title: Senior Technician
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking a Drive Unit Test Technician! You'll play a hands-on role in advancing next-generation rotating equipment and drive systems. In this fast-paced lab environment, you will perform detailed inspections, install and test drive units on dynamometers, and work closely with engineers to validate performance, reliability, and durability. You will help troubleshoot complex electromechanical challenges, build and modify test fixtures, and maintain a high level of organization and safety in the lab. If you are a mechanically skilled, detail-oriented problem solver with a passion for hands-on engineering work, and are open to supporting testing operations in the Bay Area, this role offers the opportunity to directly influence cutting-edge product development.



What You Will Do 

 - Perform both visual and functional evaluations of rotating equipment
   (motor/engine) and related components to identify defects, inconsistencies,
   and areas for improvement

 - Install drive units onto Dynamometers, conduct testing, and assess
   prototype performance to confirm design assumptions and highlight
   process improvement opportunities

 - Partner with test engineers to develop and execute test procedures, plans,
   and methodologies for verifying drive unit functionality, reliability and
   durability.

 - Coordinate with cross-functional teams —design, reliability, and testing—to
   troubleshoot technical challenges and contribute to design refinement

 - Document test result, inspection reports, and technical observations clearly
   and thoroughly to support informed engineering decisions

 - Maintain a high standard of organization and safety in the lab, including
   inventory, tooling, and equipment maintenance

 - Design, fabricate, and modify test fixtures and equipment to support drive
   system testing and validation

 - Be open to travel to support testing operations in the Bay Area



What You Will Bring 

 - High school diploma or GED required; hands-on technical training or
   certification in automotive, electrical, or similar fields is a plus

 - Strong hands-on background in a comparable role, with a deep
   understanding of engineering concepts and applications

 - Skilled in mechanical assembly and fabrication, with proficiency in
   machine shop tools and expert use of hand/power tools
    1000V HV awareness

 - Capable of independently disassembling and reassembling
   electromechanical assemblies

 - Comfortable using standard lab instruments such as multimeters, DAQ
   systems, and power supplies

 - Experience with wiring harness design and fabrication, including
   soldering, crimping, and following wiring diagrams

 - Strong understanding of physics and engineering fundamentals, with the
   ability to apply principles to solve complex problems

 - Excellent documentation and written communication skills, with
   proficiency in Microsoft Office

 - Exposure to LabVIEW, Python, or equivalent is a plus

 - Ability to lift up to 50 lbs., with frequent standing, walking, and bending in
   a fast-paced lab environment



The pay for this position ranges from $45.00 to $60.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

In this role, you will be a member of Also’s Technical Program Management team, responsible for driving the drive unit and actuator modules end to end from concept/proto development phase through mass production. You will partner with product, mechanical, electrical, firmware, test, supply chain, industrial design, and other cross-functional teams to drive product development in consumer-facing products.



What You Will Do 

 - As a Technical Program Manager, you’ll use your product development expertise to lead multi-disciplinary hardware projects from start to finish: managing drive unit programs from architecture and prototyping through validation, industrialization and production ramp.

 - You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify and manage risks early leading to rapid reaction plans to keep the program on track, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company.

 - Drive the planning and implementation of customer features with the cross-functional teams to hit roadmap goals, tracking progress, while communicating status, blockers, and risks to leadership.

 - Develop and manage comprehensive program schedules via Gantt charts, technical issues, design release management, certification, manufacturing, and resource needs with engineering, supply chain, and cross-functional teams.

 - Identify and solve the top program blockers and adapt lean processes to the organization.



What You Will Bring 

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, or a related engineering field

 - 7+ years of experience in program management, engineering or similar cross-functional role

 - Demonstrated success in shipping drive unit and actuator products from initial concept through mass production.

 - Familiarity with New Product Introduction (NPI) processes, including tooling qualification, PPAP, DVT/PVT, and first-article inspections.

 - Experience managing programs involving electromechanical systems with multiple interdependent subsystems (motors, PCBAs, sensors, structural assemblies).

 - Experience working directly with contract manufacturers and global suppliers on industrialization and production readiness.

 - Ability to understand technical discussions (driven by curiosity to understand how the entire system works) and provide decision framework to make technical decisions and accelerate development.

 - Clear communicator - able to hold conversations with engineering and supply chain while distilling status and decisions for executive leadership.

The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $250,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.

•Must be able to effectively lead and facilitate meetings with customers and technical team members.

title: Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Precision Medicine (PMed) Immunology and Neuroscience organization at AbbVie uses advanced methods to discover biomarkers and implement translational strategies to advance AbbVie’s innovative Immunology and Neuroscience pipeline.
The Associate Director, Biomarker Program Management, leads a team within the Immunology and Neuroscience therapeutic area that connects science and operations to manage biomarker research for multiple Phase 1-3 clinical trials. This role provides vision for operational and logistical strategies to ensure clinical trials are executed with quality and efficiency, on-time, within budget, and meet objectives. The Associate Director achieves these objectives via scientific expertise, strategic thinking, a global mindset, team building and cross-functional collaboration. This role can be based in North Chicago, IL, Waltham, MA, or South San Francisco, CA.
Responsibilities:
Lead team of Biomarker Project Managers and Sample Operations Managers to facilitate the implementation of PMed research into AbbVie clinical trials. Provide management and mentoring for team members; responsible for developing the expertise of team members. Set a positive and motivating work environment that encourages mutual respect, innovation, and accountability at all levels.
Assign approved programs and trials to team members and ensure team members are resourced, trained, and employed to start up, manage and close clinical trials. This includes partnering with PMed Biomarker Leads and being responsible for editing clinical documents, sample management, data management, cross-functional teams, budget management and strategy documents. Programs are executed to meet required timelines, budgets, and regulatory requirements. May directly manage key clinical projects within PMed.
Manage biomarker operations and logistics to support the clinical trial schedule. Proactively identify, resolve, mitigate, and/or escalate biomarker study-related risks and issues.
Ensure vendors are managed per AbbVie procedures including selection, contract execution and management. Assist in the management of Oncology budgets, ensuring accurate projections are provided to Finance monthly, quarterly, and yearly, adjusting as appropriate to keep actual variances low.
Help set Vision for Biomarker Program Management group that enables continuous improvement in processes and efficiency. Explore potential opportunities for expanding services and capabilities of BPM. Identify gaps and spearhead special development projects, as needed.
Serve as liaison with leaders of cross-functional stakeholders within AbbVie. Responsible for collaborating with personnel in other Precision Medicine groups to drive consistency within and between groups.

description:
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/. Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
The Business Excellence Strategy group within Global Portfolio Strategy & Operations works side-by-side with the Aesthetics R&D executive team on many of the most pressing issues facing the organization, both in the short- and long-term. Work from this team will have a direct impact on the future success of AbbVie.
As an Associate Director of Business Excellence Portfolio Strategy, you will partner with leaders across AbbVie to optimize the value of our portfolio and current/future assets. The role is seeking a high performing team member who has demonstrated an interest and expertise in the biopharma industry and strong desire to advance our strategic agenda and support mission-critical assets + initiatives that will make a real difference for AbbVie’s patients. In return, the Business Excellence group will provide high profile, high impact projects and professional development experiences spanning the entire drug development value chain.
The position requires strong analytical skills and the ability to translate strategic vision into tactical action. It will be imperative in this role to identify the highest impact ideas and plans and focus efforts to work effectively in a cross-functional team.
This position is located in our Irvine, CA office (hybrid onsite days at Tues, Wed and Thurs).
Responsibilities:
•    Drive end-to-end strategic innovation, communication and execution on Allergan Aesthetics portfolio + assets in partnership with the R&D + Commercial Leadership Teams. Areas of focus include strategic planning, scenario evaluation, and data-driven problem solving spanning the breadth of drug/aesthetic medical device development.
•    Support R&D strategy processes including: Annual franchise strategy reviews and Strategy Long Range Plans, Therapeutic Area strategy and pipeline reviews, and high priority Asset Strategy Team support. This will require both strong project management and ability to generate and communicate strategic insights to leaders and franchise / asset strategy teams.
•    Support and lead strategic initiatives that address mission-critical questions and position AbbVie for future success, such as:
•   R&D competitive intelligence initiatives, including evidence-based competitive assessments, ELT scientific communications, and ongoing monitoring of key competitor activities across pipeline, scientific communications, and commercial channels
•   Dedicated strategic decision support for key pipeline assets through Asset Strategy Leader + Project & Portfolio Management partnership, governance deck development, pressure-testing of business cases, and milestone storytelling from pre-concept through pivotal trial design
•    Development and operationalization of R&D pipeline metrics and KPIs (e.g., cycle times, productivity indices, milestone tracking) for enterprise reporting, potentially including data collection, stakeholder alignment, and dashboard/visualization design
•    Structured competitive benchmarking analyses across franchises, synthesizing external best practices and internal data into actionable recommendations for R&D leadership
•    Rapid-response support to R&D leadership on high importance / visibility priorities.
•    Individual modules within complex, cross-functional initiatives, including driving the problem-solving process supporting research and analytics, and distilling pragmatic recommendations for management consideration.
•    Help communicate our strategy at executive forums across AbbVie.
•    Monitor, understand, and prioritize external trends of relevance to the enterprise, and help determine how AbbVie should prepare and/or respond.
•    Bachelors or equivalent degree required.  Advanced degree (PharmD, PhD, MD, MBA) highly preferred. 2+ years at top tier management consulting company highly preferred.
•    Minimum years of experience - 5+ with Bachelors, 3+ with Masters and 2+ with PhD.
•    Strong problem-solving skills.
•    Strong communication skills and comfortability leading meetings with senior-level management.
•    Experience managing large projects within a complex matrixed pharmaceutical organization, either as an external consultant or an internal cross-functional lead.
•    Demonstrated ability to engage senior leadership to drive alignment on a strategic vision and facilitate decision making on critical issues.
•    Capability building / Change management skills – leveraging empathy and coaching with functional stakeholders to achieve organizational buy-in and long-lasting change.

About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Position Summary
The Associate Director, Customer Engagement and Injector Training, is responsible for shaping and executing the customer engagement and injector education strategy for Chronic Migraine. This role leads the development of compliant, insight-driven education and training experiences that strengthen clinical confidence, elevate customer experience, and support brand objectives. The Associate Director works across the Therapeutic team and with cross-functional partners to translate business priorities and customer needs into high-quality, scalable programs and resources.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the annual customer engagement and injector education strategy for Chronic Migraine, aligned with brand priorities, customer insights, field needs, and the broader Neuroscience strategy.
Design, evolve, and manage an integrated portfolio of live, virtual, digital, and on-demand education and training offerings for healthcare professionals, including physicians and advanced practice providers.
Translate customer, field, and marketplace insights into program architecture, content strategy, delivery formats, and resources that improve relevance, reach, and educational impact.
Partner closely with brand marketing, sales, medical, regulatory, legal, compliance, operations, analytics, and agency partners to deliver initiatives that meet AbbVie standards and applicable policies.
Lead planning and execution for HCP engagement at priority national and regional society meetings and professional organizations, in coordination with internal stakeholders.
Oversee speaker and trainer strategy and operations, including faculty identification, contracting, training, content readiness, program quality, and compliant execution.
Build strong relationships with external experts, customers, professional societies, field leaders, and cross-functional partners to ensure programs address evolving clinical and business needs.
Develop annual operating plans, forecasts, and budgets; manage agency and vendor performance, scope, timelines, and spend with disciplined stewardship.
Establish meaningful performance indicators and reporting to assess program reach, experience, quality, and business contribution; use insights to optimize the portfolio and recommend enhancements.
Anticipate changes in adult learning, customer engagement, digital education, and the therapeutic toxin landscape; identify and pilot innovative approaches that can be scaled responsibly.
Communicate strategy, progress, risks, and recommendations clearly to cross-functional teams and senior leadership while managing multiple high-priority initiatives in a matrixed environment.
Travel to selected customer programs, field engagements, and professional meetings as needed.
Leadership and Collaboration
Influence without direct authority and create alignment across diverse functions, priorities, and perspectives.
Demonstrate enterprise leadership, sound judgment, accountability, and a strong commitment to integrity and compliance.
Champion an inclusive, customer-centered culture and proactively share best practices across Therapeutics and AbbVie.
Provide clear direction to agency and vendor partners and foster a high standard of quality, innovation, and execution
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution; Advanced degree from an accredited institution preferred.
Five or more years of combined experience in pharmaceutical or biotechnology marketing, HCP education, customer engagement, sales, sales training, or a related commercial function.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing strategic plans and complex, cross-functional programs.
Experience managing budgets, agencies, vendors, timelines, and multiple concurrent workstreams.
Strong written, verbal, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to use qualitative and quantitative insights to guide decisions and optimize customer experiences.
Demonstrated ability to lead through change, operate effectively in a fast-paced matrix environment, and influence across levels and functions.
Ability to travel up to 40%.

Purpose
The Associate Director, Customs Valuation Compliance & Reporting, is a critical compliance role that actively partners across the enterprise and leads the operations and strategic design of the end-to-end customs valuation and reconciliation process.  Responsibilities include leading the financial planning and reporting of customs tariff impact to AbbVie’s imports (primarily focused on the Americas region) by conducting relevant variance analyses, scenario modeling and developing executive-ready reports; leading customs valuation initiatives in collaboration with stakeholders from other departments; and ensuring accuracy and predictability of tariff costs and other customs reporting metrics.

Develop and manage the program governance and controls for key trade program strategies for AbbVie
Primary SME on the review of contracts to determine potential customs valuation considerations (e.g., royalties)
Manage resource(s) supporting the existing customs valuation processes and strategies
Participate in governance forums and interface with various levels of leadership
Advise and support cross-functional activities as new tariff regulations are enacted

Ability to recognize opportunities to simplify processes and create efficiencies

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. The Data Governance Specialist supports the consistent and timely operation of the Gov360 governance process across R&D. The role receives, assesses, processes, and triages Gov360 requests; determines the appropriate governance pathway; coordinates required reviews with business and functional partners; and maintains complete, accurate, and traceable records. The position also improves processes, updates guidance and training materials, delivers user education, and partners with subject-matter experts to define and operationalize high-risk use cases and escalation criteria. Through disciplined case management, practical guidance, metrics, and continuous improvement, the role helps simplify governance for users while ensuring requests are handled in alignment with established standards, procedures, and risk-based decision making.
Responsibilities:
Receive, assess, process, and triage Gov360 requests, confirming completeness, clarifying business needs, identifying dependencies, and routing each request to the appropriate governance pathway or subject-matter expert.
Perform initial risk-based assessments using established criteria; identify requests that may require enhanced review, escalation, additional controls, or cross-functional input.
Manage assigned requests through completion by coordinating stakeholder input, tracking decisions and action items, maintaining status, and following up on open items to support timely resolution.
Partner with Legal, Privacy, Information Security, Quality, Compliance, Data, AI, and R&D business representatives, as applicable, to define and maintain high-risk use cases, decision criteria, required evidence, and escalation triggers.
Maintain accurate, complete, and audit-ready records in Gov360, including request documentation, assessments, decisions, conditions, approvals, supporting evidence, and closure information.
Analyze recurring questions, case trends, bottlenecks, and user feedback; recommend and implement practical process improvements that reduce burden, eliminate unnecessary steps, improve consistency, and strengthen the user experience.
Create, revise, and maintain Gov360 procedures, work instructions, job aids, templates, FAQs, decision trees, and other guidance so they remain clear, current, and aligned with approved governance requirements.
Develop and deliver role-based Gov360 training, onboarding, office hours, and targeted communications for requestors, reviewers, and governance partners; assess training needs and incorporate lessons learned.
Prepare and monitor operational metrics, dashboards, and reports covering request volume, status, cycle time, aging, outcomes, escalations, and recurring risk themes; highlight issues requiring management attention.
Support governance program initiatives, system or workflow enhancements, user acceptance testing, inspection or audit readiness, and other continuous-improvement activities as assigned.
Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in law, risk management, or related field. An advanced degree or relevant certification is preferred.
Typically 1-2 years of relevant experience in data governance, information governance, risk assessment, compliance, quality, business operations, process management, or a related area; pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, or another regulated-industry experience is preferred.
Experience using structured workflows or case-management systems to assess requests, maintain documentation, coordinate reviews, and track actions through closure.
Working knowledge of data-governance concepts, risk-based assessment, data lifecycle practices, privacy, security, quality, compliance, and responsible use of data or AI. Deep expertise in every domain is not required.
Demonstrated ability to interpret requirements and translate them into clear operational guidance, decision criteria, job aids, and training materials.

title: Information Research M&A Integration Lead
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Our Business Technology Solutions (BTS) team through digital transformation accelerates the future of medicine at AbbVie—and we do it together, asking bold questions and taking on tough challenges through deep, honest collaboration. In the role of  Information Research (IR) Mergers & Acquisition (M&A) Integration Lead , key member of the IR Integration Management Office (IMO), you will join a diverse, global team that invests in your customized career growth and uses technology and data to positively impact people’s lives.
This role represents the BTS-Information Research (IR) organization as the overall IR M&A Integration Lead working directly with cross-functional R&D business and cross-functional BTS teams to execute deal transactions to further grow AbbVie’s Therapeutic Areas. This role performs as the primary IR M&A Integration Lead responsible for planning and executing deals addressing cross-functional dependencies to achieve AbbVie’s desired end-state operating model as we integrate or divest companies.
For anyone who wants to use technology and data to make a difference in people’s lives, shape the digital transformation of a leading biopharmaceutical company, and secure sustainable career growth within a diverse, global team – we are ready for you. In this role, you can expect competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits for every career stage and a commitment to your well-being in the workplace. Additionally, you will add your unique experience to an employee-driven culture with vibrant Employee Resource Groups and a passion for equity, equality, inclusion, and diversity that reflects the diversity of our communities and the patients and customers we serve.
Mergers & Acquisitions (M&As) include multiple types of transactions that require BTS and IR leadership. M&A transactions include R&D Ventures, Partnerships & Alliances, Co-Promotion, Co-Development, Divesting Products and/or Sites, Plant Acquisitions and Divestitures, and Full Company Acquisitions.
This is a critical role in partnering with leadership to further define the strategy to evolve BTS’s M&A organization, services, and playbooks for the various types of M&A deals.  This will include cross-functional engagement and leadership across the BTS organization and working with AbbVie’s business leaders, Search and Evaluation, Business Development, and our Transition Office.
Responsibilities:
​​Perform as the IR M&A Integration Lead over multiple AbbVie company-wide and R&D deal transactions responsible for overall program health, financials, and reporting.
​For each deal, establish the cross-functional IR team fully accountable to integrate or divest people, data, and systems.
​Develop business relationships and integrate activities with other BTOs to ensure successful integration execution and support of project efforts into long term execution. Manage relationships between BTOs, R&D Business, and Finance to ensure effective communication between the groups is occurring. Broker services within BTS on behalf of customers; coordinate portfolio of solutions and identify interdependencies.
​Work with the R&D business and BTS functional leads to clearly define business decisions, solution options and recommendations for a given deal based on deal model, size, complexity, risk, and speed to business value.
​Ally with other BTOs to remain current on project status and inform management and stakeholders of progress; conversely, keep managers and stakeholders aware of user issues and resolve conflicts proactively.
​Responsible for escalating and driving risks and issues cross-functionally.
​Present IR updates in IR Leadership forums and R&D Integration Forums
Responsible for ​continuous improvement projects to drive speed and agility in BTS M&A services and capabilities. Identify and implement AI innovative solutions and capabilities to challenge status quo and bring value to the business faster.
​Responsible for compliance with BTS’s SLC, Corporate and Divisional policies and procedures.​​
Create AI agents and tools to reimagine or improve a process or capability. Lead and implement multiple projects that drive speed, efficiencies, and/or cost savings.
Effectively influence leaders and cross functional teams without direct authority.
Present BTS updates to the function VPs in the Steering Committees and leadership forums.

The role combines ownership of high-complexity campaign work with formal people leadership, technical oversight, and cross-functional partnership.
Responsibilities include:
Build, QC, and execute high-complexity brand omnichannel programs. This includes building journeys (base cadences) and highly complex trigger programs that deliver the right message to the right person at the right time through the right channel.
Ensure high-quality, on-time, and error-free implementation, testing, and QA of campaigns within the marketing automation platform. Create, review, and share standard quality-control documents and follow the process to ensure accuracy and completeness.
Lead and manage assigned team members, including day-to-day work allocation and prioritization, coaching, performance management, development planning, onboarding, and quality oversight. Maintain a focused campaign workload that allows appropriate attention to people leadership and team delivery.
Monitor email deliverability across domains for all brand campaigns implemented. Provide recommendations on how to optimize deliverability, resolve IP reputation issues, and ensure proper inbox placement.
Identify issues, determine root cause, and recommend corrective action for campaign builds, data and audience logic, IP reputation, deliverability, and operational processes.
Participate in and lead agile delivery activities such as design, build, QA, and continuous improvement. Maintain documents per department document-management policies and procedures.
Influence and implement capabilities including targeting, personalization, audience segmentation, journey orchestration, and dynamic content to deliver the best customer experience. Build and execute test plans, identify winners, and proactively recommend optimization opportunities that improve deliverability, reach, and engagement.
Lead internal and external partners to define, execute, and optimize email, direct mail, media, and omnichannel campaigns. Lead or contribute to team innovations, cross-functional projects, and scalable process improvements. Partners include Brand Marketing, Strategy, Business Technology Solutions, Marketing Analytics and Business Insights, Creative, Digital Agencies, and other CRM and technology teams.
Provide exemplary customer service while setting, maintaining, and exceeding stakeholder expectations. Communicate progress, decisions, stakeholder alignment, risks, and business value to the Associate Director and other partners.
Keep abreast of 1:1 marketing, CRM, email industry best practices, and new technology through professional organizations, seminars, and conferences. Recommend practical applications to the Associate Director.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, or equivalent experience.
5–8 years of experience in database marketing, CRM, email, digital, direct mail, marketing automation, or 1:1 marketing.
Minimum of 5 years of hands-on experience creating campaigns in enterprise-level marketing automation platforms. Strong Adobe Marketo Engage experience is preferred; experience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Journey Optimizer, or similar platforms is also valued. Platform certification or equivalent demonstrated enterprise experience is preferred.

AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated person to join the Biologics CMC Developability Team. Our team utilizes state-of-the-art biophysical and analytical instrumentation to assess candidates coming out of the Discovery pipeline. title: Senior Director, Pipeline Market Access Strategy - Immunology
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Senior Director, Pipeline Market Access Strategy (PMAX) is a newly created role responsible for leading and inspiring the end-to-end global market access strategy for pipeline assets within their assigned Business Unit. This position will require strong enterprise leadership to navigate the organization through multiple external environment pressures on global pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement.
This role bridges early asset development and future commercialization readiness, ensuring that pricing and access considerations are embedded from the earliest stages of the drug development lifecycle and through Phase 3 design and identification of evidence needs. The Senior Director serves as the definitive voice of pipeline market access, shaping clinical trial design, evidence generation, and target product profiles through a global access and reimbursement lens.  Importantly this position will need to define distinct US and international strategies to optimize global launch success.
The Senior Director will lead a team of experts across both US Pipeline Strategy and International Pipeline Strategy and will have an opportunity to define the objectives and vision for the team appropriately.  This role will provide leadership across both domestic and global dimensions of pipeline access, partnering deeply with inline US and International access teams as well as R&D, Regulatory, HEOR, Global Commercial Development, Business Development, and Government Affairs to deliver integrated access strategies that position AbbVie's pipeline for long-term commercial and patient-access success.
Key Responsibilities
Pipeline Access Strategy & Portfolio Leadership
Owns the end-to-end pipeline Integrated access strategy for all pre-launch and development-stage assets within the assigned Business Unit, ensuring strategies are comprehensive in addressing evidence needs, policy considerations, pricing potential, and commercial considerations. IASs integrate global needs and dynamics through regulatory submission.
Serves as the primary voice of pipeline market access strategies at Business Unit governance forums, including LMG, TASC, CSM,  ASTs , and other senior leadership reviews — communicating access risk, opportunity, and strategic direction with clarity and conviction.
Serves as the voice of access into pipeline Business Development opportunities.
Leads prioritization exercises across the pipeline portfolio to ensure resources and strategic attention are allocated to assets with the greatest near- and long-term access complexity and business impact.
Creates and optimizes launch strategies inclusive of considerations for IRA, MFN, and other market forces (US Channel dynamics) to position the asset for sequencing strategies across indications as well as geographies incorporating the pressures
Defines and delivers the Access Roadmap— a cross-functionally developed strategy that articulates the access approach for each pipeline asset by development phase, anticipated launch timing, and global evidence deliverables.
Early Development Integration
Partners with R&D and Regulatory teams to embed access-relevant endpoints, comparators, and trial design elements into clinical development programs from Phase I/II onward — ensuring studies are powered to meet payer and HTA evidence standards at launch and partners with the affiliates.
Defines and champions Target Product Profiles (TPPs) from a market access perspective, translating payer value requirements into actionable clinical and evidence generation guidance for asset teams.
Generates and maintains global payer and HTA evidence requirements across major markets (US, EU5, Japan, and emerging markets), ensuring development programs proactively address the evidence gaps that govern access and reimbursement decisions.
US & International Strategy Alignment
Provides strategic leadership and direction to the US Pipeline Strategy Lead and International Pipeline Strategy Lead, ensuring both domestic and global perspectives are fully integrated into a cohesive, Business Unit-level pipeline access strategy.
Aligns US payer strategy, formulary positioning, and value communication frameworks with international HTA, pricing, and reimbursement approaches — creating a globally consistent access narrative that can flex to local market requirements.
Anticipates cross-market reference pricing dynamics, parallel trade risks, and HTA precedent effects, incorporating these considerations into early pipeline access strategy to protect long-term portfolio value across geographies.
Partners closely with US and International Pipeline Strategy Leads to develop and execute a structured pipeline-to-launch transition framework, ensuring that market access strategies, payer evidence packages, and reimbursement submissions are fully prepared ahead of regulatory approval.
Collaborates with US and international commercial, medical, and market access teams to ensure seamless knowledge transfer and strategic handoff at the point of regulatory approval — including payer communication plans, launch sequencing strategies, and country-level access readiness assessments.
Leads cross-functional launch readiness reviews in partnership with US and International teams to identify and resolve access gaps (evidence, pricing approvals, formulary positioning) prior to approval, ensuring no delays to patient access at launch.
Ensures that affiliate and in-country market access teams are equipped with globally aligned value messages, health economic tools, and reimbursement dossiers well in advance of launch — bridging the transition from pipeline to commercial ownership.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Partnership
Provides strategic direction and partnership to cross-functional groups including HEOR, R&D, Regulatory, Global Commercial Development, Global Marketing, Government Affairs, and Business Development — ensuring market access perspectives are fully integrated into all pipeline asset decisions.
Leads the development of Integrated Evidence Plans (IEPs) in close collaboration with HEOR, ensuring real-world evidence, health economic modeling, and outcomes research strategies are aligned with anticipated payer and HTA requirements at launch.
Partners with Government Affairs to anticipate and shape the evolving policy and reimbursement landscape, embedding policy risk and opportunity assessments into pipeline access strategies.
Collaborates with Global Commercial Development and Global Marketing to ensure pipeline access strategies are aligned with brand positioning, indication sequencing, and long-range commercial forecasts.
Business Development & Asset Evaluation
Works closely with Business Development to inform the market access potential of in-licensing, partnership, and acquisition opportunities — providing rigorous payer landscape assessments, reimbursement probability analyses, and access risk evaluations to support BD decision-making.
Establishes and communicates access-based licensing priorities, ensuring that pipeline expansion decisions account for payer value evidence requirements, competitive access dynamics, and global pricing sustainability.
Serves as the access subject matter expert in due diligence processes, assessing the payer readiness and evidence maturity of externally sourced pipeline assets being evaluated for AbbVie's portfolio.
Governance, Stakeholder Engagement & People Leadership
Represents pipeline market access priorities at senior leadership governance forums, portfolio review committees, and cross-Business Unit strategy sessions — serving as the definitive voice on access considerations that should inform pipeline investment and development decisions.
Builds, develops, and retains a high-performing pipeline access team, providing mentorship, career development, and performance management for direct and indirect reports across US and international functions.
Fosters a culture of innovation, rigor, and affiliate-centricity within the pipeline access team — ensuring that affiliate launch needs, in-country market dynamics, and local payer requirements are actively incorporated into global strategy development.
Education
An advanced degree (MBA, MPH, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) in business, health economics, public policy, life sciences, or a related field is required.
Formal training or demonstrated expertise in health technology assessment (HTA), health economics, outcomes research, or pharmaceutical development is strongly preferred.
Bachelor's degree in a scientific, business, or public health discipline is required as a minimum baseline.
Experience
A minimum of 12–15 years of progressive, senior-level experience in market access, pricing, reimbursement, HEOR, or a closely related pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical function — with a substantial portion of that experience focused on pipeline and pre-launch strategy.
Demonstrated expertise in global market access, including a deep working knowledge of HTA processes, payer evidence requirements, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and access decision-making dynamics across major international markets (US, EU5, Japan, and additional key markets).
Proven experience shaping clinical development strategy from a market access and outcomes evidence perspective — including direct experience contributing to clinical trial design, endpoint selection, and Integrated Evidence Plan development in collaboration with R&D teams.
Strong track record of leading and developing high-performing teams in a matrixed, multinational environment, with demonstrated ability to manage direct reports and influence cross-functional partners without direct authority.
Experience supporting Business Development activities including asset due diligence, licensing evaluations, and access-based valuation assessments is highly preferred.
Comfortable operating at the senior leadership level, with demonstrated ability to communicate complex access strategy to executive audiences and influence enterprise-level pipeline investment decisions.
Experience across multiple therapeutic areas (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Neuroscience) is an asset, though deep expertise in at least one is required.
Key Competencies
Strategic Vision & Access Leadership
Global HTA & Payer Expertise
Clinical Development Partnership
Evidence Generation Strategy
Cross-Functional Influence
Pipeline Portfolio Prioritization
Business Development Acumen
US/International Strategy Alignment
People Leadership & Talent Development
Executive Communication & Governance

Pipeline Access Strategy & Portfolio Leadership
Owns the end-to-end pipeline Integrated access strategy for all pre-launch and development-stage assets within the assigned Business Unit, ensuring strategies are comprehensive in addressing evidence needs, policy considerations, pricing potential, and commercial considerations. Serves as the primary voice of pipeline market access strategies at Business Unit governance forums, including LMG, TASC, CSM,  ASTs , and other senior leadership reviews — communicating access risk, opportunity, and strategic direction with clarity and conviction.
Serves as the voice of access into pipeline Business Development opportunities.
Leads prioritization exercises across the pipeline portfolio to ensure resources and strategic attention are allocated to assets with the greatest near- and long-term access complexity and business impact.
Creates and optimizes launch strategies inclusive of considerations for IRA, MFN, and other market forces (US Channel dynamics) to position the asset for sequencing strategies across indications as well as geographies incorporating the pressures

Early Development Integration
Partners with R&D and Regulatory teams to embed access-relevant endpoints, comparators, and trial design elements into clinical development programs from Phase I/II onward — ensuring studies are powered to meet payer and HTA evidence standards at launch and partners with the affiliates.

Aligns US payer strategy, formulary positioning, and value communication frameworks with international HTA, pricing, and reimbursement approaches — creating a globally consistent access narrative that can flex to local market requirements.
Anticipates cross-market reference pricing dynamics, parallel trade risks, and HTA precedent effects, incorporating these considerations into early pipeline access strategy to protect long-term portfolio value across geographies.

Leads cross-functional launch readiness reviews in partnership with US and International teams to identify and resolve access gaps (evidence, pricing approvals, formulary positioning) prior to approval, ensuring no delays to patient access at launch.
Ensures that affiliate and in-country market access teams are equipped with globally aligned value messages, health economic tools, and reimbursement dossiers well in advance of launch — bridging the transition from pipeline to commercial ownership.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Partnership
Provides strategic direction and partnership to cross-functional groups including HEOR, R&D, Regulatory, Global Commercial Development, Global Marketing, Government Affairs, and Business Development — ensuring market access perspectives are fully integrated into all pipeline asset decisions.
Leads the development of Integrated Evidence Plans (IEPs) in close collaboration with HEOR, ensuring real-world evidence, health economic modeling, and outcomes research strategies are aligned with anticipated payer and HTA requirements at launch.
Partners with Government Affairs to anticipate and shape the evolving policy and reimbursement landscape, embedding policy risk and opportunity assessments into pipeline access strategies.
Collaborates with Global Commercial Development and Global Marketing to ensure pipeline access strategies are aligned with brand positioning, indication sequencing, and long-range commercial forecasts.
Business Development & Asset Evaluation
Works closely with Business Development to inform the market access potential of in-licensing, partnership, and acquisition opportunities — providing rigorous payer landscape assessments, reimbursement probability analyses, and access risk evaluations to support BD decision-making.
Establishes and communicates access-based licensing priorities, ensuring that pipeline expansion decisions account for payer value evidence requirements, competitive access dynamics, and global pricing sustainability.
Serves as the access subject matter expert in due diligence processes, assessing the payer readiness and evidence maturity of externally sourced pipeline assets being evaluated for AbbVie's portfolio.
Governance, Stakeholder Engagement & People Leadership
Represents pipeline market access priorities at senior leadership governance forums, portfolio review committees, and cross-Business Unit strategy sessions — serving as the definitive voice on access considerations that should inform pipeline investment and development decisions.
Builds, develops, and retains a high-performing pipeline access team, providing mentorship, career development, and performance management for direct and indirect reports across US and international functions.
Fosters a culture of innovation, rigor, and affiliate-centricity within the pipeline access team — ensuring that affiliate launch needs, in-country market dynamics, and local payer requirements are actively incorporated into global strategy development.
Education
An advanced degree (MBA, MPH, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent) in business, health economics, public policy, life sciences, or a related field is required.
Formal training or demonstrated expertise in health technology assessment (HTA), health economics, outcomes research, or pharmaceutical development is strongly preferred.
Bachelor's degree in a scientific, business, or public health discipline is required as a minimum baseline.

A minimum of 12–15 years of progressive, senior-level experience in market access, pricing, reimbursement, HEOR, or a closely related pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical function — with a substantial portion of that experience focused on pipeline and pre-launch strategy.
Demonstrated expertise in global market access, including a deep working knowledge of HTA processes, payer evidence requirements, pricing and reimbursement frameworks, and access decision-making dynamics across major international markets (US, EU5, Japan, and additional key markets).
Proven experience shaping clinical development strategy from a market access and outcomes evidence perspective — including direct experience contributing to clinical trial design, endpoint selection, and Integrated Evidence Plan development in collaboration with R&D teams.
Strong track record of leading and developing high-performing teams in a matrixed, multinational environment, with demonstrated ability to manage direct reports and influence cross-functional partners without direct authority.

Develop SAS programs for the creation of ADaM data sets following CDISC standards.
Develop SAS programs for the creation of Tables, Listings and Figures.
Validation of ADaM data sets. Validation of Tables, Listings and Figures.
Create specifications for the structure of ADaM data sets for individual studies and integrated data
Minimum Qualifications:
MS in Statistics, Computer Science or a related field with 2+ years of relevant experience. OR BS in Statistics, Computer Science or a related field with 4+ years of relevant experience.
Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials
Demonstrated practical understanding of SAS programming related to drug development.
Experience creating and reviewing ADaM datasets for analysis
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated ability to support efficacy analyses across clinical development phases and therapeutic areas.
Other Required Skills:
Ability to communicate clearly both oral and written.

Basic understanding of the drug development process.

Help meet the technology needs of External Innovation teams within the Corporate Business & Strategy Office (CBSO). As part of the BTS Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) team, you will be dedicated to supporting these teams’ technology needs.
Design and deliver technology and AI-enabled solutions to complex business challenges. You will partner with business and technology stakeholders to understand their challenges and translate their needs into technical requirements.
As a technical expert, you will independently design, develop, integrate, test, and validate complex solutions. You will apply your expertise to translate emerging technologies into practical business outcomes.
You will bring knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, large language models (LLMs), machine learning concepts, AI governance, and responsible AI practices.

Opportunity Discovery: Partner with CBSO External Innovation stakeholders and BTS M&A teams to identify business problems, assess where AI adds value, and prioritize high-impact opportunities.
AI Prototyping: Build and demonstrate AI prototypes using approved code, AI services, automation tools, application programming interfaces, and enterprise data.
Technical Compliance: Apply AbbVie standards for secure software delivery, responsible AI, privacy, data protection, change management, and the software development lifecycle.

Business Analysis: Translate business needs into user stories, process flows, requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Delivery Leadership: Lead AI initiatives from discovery through delivery and adoption, including priorities, release outcomes, dependencies, risks, testing, and acceptance.
Risk & Change Management: Manage delivery risks, issues, changes, and stakeholder communications.
Production Readiness: Partner with architecture, engineering, security, privacy, and platform teams to turn successful prototypes into secure, maintainable solutions.
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Life Sciences, or a related discipline plus 5 years of experience; or a Master’s Degree plus 4 years of experience.
AI Solution Delivery: Hands-on experience designing, coding, testing, and demonstrating AI-enabled solutions, including generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation, workflow automation, intelligent agents, or similar capabilities.
Applied AI Knowledge: Practical knowledge of generative AI, large language models, prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, AI copilots, agentic AI, machine learning fundamentals, responsible AI, data quality, privacy, security, implementation risks, and limitations.
Technical Toolkit: Proficiency in Python or another modern programming language, with familiarity using cloud platforms, containers, application programming interfaces, and enterprise integration patterns to build and troubleshoot working solutions.
Consulting & Technical Experience: Ability to gather ambiguous business requirements and translate them into clear user stories, functional requirements, technical requirements, and acceptance criteria. Hands-on experience designing, prototyping, testing, or implementing AI-enabled or other technology solutions.
Value Translation: Experience turning a business problem into a working solution and explaining its value, limitations, and implementation considerations to stakeholders.
Delivery Methods: Understanding of software development lifecycle methods, Agile practices, and modern product delivery approaches.
Problem Solving & Communication: Ability to learn quickly, solve ambiguous technical problems, collaborate across teams, and explain technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.

description:
The Opportunity
Adobe’s Risk Advisory & Assurance Services (RAAS) team is seeking a Senior Manager to lead our IT SOX compliance program and ensure the technology controls supporting financial reporting are well-designed, effective, and scalable.
This role requires deep expertise in IT SOX and IT general controls, including SAP and cloud environments, along with a solid grasp of enterprise systems, data flows, and end-to-end business processes.
Partnering with the Senior Director, RAAS, you will manage the IT SOX program. You will engage with IT, Finance, control owners, co-sourced testing providers, and external auditors to ensure the program remains efficient and effective.
How You Will Make an Impact
Strategic Partnership
Serve as a trusted advisor to IT, Finance, and business leaders, building strong relationships and applying forward-looking technology risk judgment to anticipate change, identify emerging risks, and shape decisions.
Represent IT SOX within Adobe's broader assurance landscape, aligning with second-line and other assurance teams to reduce duplication and strengthen overall risk coverage.
IT SOX Program Ownership
Own the IT SOX compliance program from planning and scoping through testing, remediation, and reporting, setting the annual audit strategy alongside SOX PMO, Finance, IT control owners, our co-sourced provider, and external auditors.
Continually reshape the IT SOX roadmap and operating model, including capability and resourcing needs, to stay ahead of changes in Adobe's business and technology landscape rather than reacting to them.
Be the trusted counterpart for our external auditor on IT SOX matters, shaping scope, reliance, testing approach, and evidence expectations to raise efficiency without giving up assurance quality.
Own IT control deficiencies going beyond symptoms to root cause, weighing severity and financial risk, and validating that remediation actually holds up and prevents recurrence.
Systems, Controls & Technical Judgment
Understand Adobe's financial systems, data, and cloud architecture from infrastructure to finance applications to know which controls matter most.
Get ahead of major business and technology transformations by embedding risk and control thinking into the build rather than adding it retroactively.
Automation, Innovation & Training
Drive automation, analytics, and continuous monitoring to improve program effectiveness, and assess how AI and automation affect the control environment.
Train control owners and business partners on SOX responsibilities and control design, building control awareness across the organization over time.
People Leadership & Coaching
Coach and develop audit professionals through clear priorities, feedback, growth opportunities, and leadership development.
Build an inclusive, high-accountability culture focused on quality, collaboration, and continuous learning.
What you need to succeed
Experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field.
CPA, CISA, CIA, CISSP, or equivalent professional certification preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience related to IT SOX, IT audit, or technology risk, ideally including Big Four or large public company experience.
Hands-on experience with SAP environments, including SAP security, controls, and integration with SOX compliance programs. Experience with cloud technology and cloud control environments is strongly preferred.
Experience managing outsourced or co-sourced audit relationships and coordinating with external auditors.
People leadership experience in developing and growing a team.

Solid understanding of IT general and application controls (ITGC/ITAC), the COSO framework, and SOX 404 requirements.
Ability to reason about system architecture and data flows to make sound control scoping decisions across the technology stack.
Ability to apply data analytics and automation to audit and control design.
Strong root cause analysis and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward durable remediation over short-term fixes.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills, able to translate complex technical and control topics into clear, actionable guidance.
High degree of integrity, sound judgment, and professional skepticism.

description:

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
THE COMMUNITY YOU WILL JOIN
Airbnb's Marketing Technology organization builds the infrastructure that powers how we reach and connect with guests and hosts around the world — from audience segmentation and campaign orchestration to last-mile delivery and real-time insights. Our engineers work at the intersection of scale, reliability, and product impact, building platforms that carry billions of messages each year across email, SMS, push, and WhatsApp. We are deeply committed to building AI-natively: agents and LLM-powered automation are becoming core to how we build, operate, and improve our systems.
You'll lead two closely partnered teams that together own Airbnb's communications platform end to end. The Orchestration team builds the systems that let marketing and product teams design and run personalized, event- and list-triggered customer journeys at Airbnb scale. The Delivery team owns the last mile — routing every notification through the right provider, tracking it to a terminal state, and managing contact preferences and vendor relationships. Both teams collaborate deeply with audience segmentation, content, ML, and data engineering teams, as well as product partners across the company.
THE DIFFERENCE YOU WILL MAKE
As the Engineering Manager for this team, you will be the primary technical leader for the systems that decide whether a message reaches a guest or host — and when. You'll set the technical direction, own roadmap execution, and build the kind of team culture where engineers grow and do the best work of their careers, including through deep, genuine adoption of AI-native engineering practices.
The platform is mid-transformation. We are consolidating legacy and next-generation messaging flows onto a single unified path, moving platform health from component metrics to business-impact signals such as campaign delivery SLAs and burn rate, and building end-to-end observability so any owner — human or agent — can answer "what happened to notification X for user Y" in minutes. At the same time, both teams are standing up agentic capabilities: an agent-driven orchestration layer, end-to-end lifecycle testing agents, smart notification scheduling, and AI-assisted on-call triage. You will be the leader who ensures these systems ship with the rigor, reliability, and operational maturity that production-grade messaging and agentic systems demand.
Your leadership will directly determine how reliably Airbnb communicates with its community, how confidently partner teams can build on the platform, and how effectively this team leads Marketing Technology's shift toward AI-native engineering.

Lead planning, roadmap reviews, and cross-team syncs for Delivery and Orchestration, keeping delivery on track and stakeholders well-informed
Run 1:1s with engineers across both teams, with intentional focus on career growth, technical skill development, and early identification of blockers
Serve as the primary engineering point of contact for cross-team dependencies — fielding requests from product teams across Airbnb and making clear, reasoned prioritization calls
Partner with the Product Manager to sequence the roadmap across journey orchestration, bulk campaign sends, and delivery infrastructure
Drive technical strategy for end-to-end observability and SLA-driven delivery: campaign-level delivery tracking, health-gated ramping, dynamic pacing against budgets, and automatic provider failover
Oversee the design, delivery, and operational health of production agentic systems: agent-driven orchestration, lifecycle testing agents, smart scheduling, and LLM-assisted on-call triage
Champion AI-native development practices across both teams — from AI-assisted coding and review to agents in CI/CD, on-call response, and delivery anomaly detection
Own the health and operational maturity of both teams: daytime and 24/7 on-call programs, blameless incident retrospectives, SLO definitions, runbook quality, and third-party messaging vendor escalations
Represent the communications platform in org-wide planning cycles and contribute to the broader Marketing Technology engineering strategy
YOUR EXPERTISE
Required
5+ years of software engineering experience, with 4+ years in an engineering management role leading platform or infrastructure teams
Demonstrated AI-native engineering mindset — you use AI tools daily in your own work, have led teams in genuinely adopting AI-assisted development, and have strong opinions about where agents add real leverage vs. hype
Experience leading teams that have designed, built, and operated production-grade agentic systems — autonomous or semi-autonomous agent pipelines, LLM-orchestrated workflows, or multi-agent architectures handling real production traffic
Strong technical foundation in high-throughput distributed systems: event-driven architectures, message queues and streaming (Kafka or similar), workflow orchestration engines (Temporal or similar), and multi-provider integrations — able to engage credibly in architecture and design conversations
Track record of running reliable, customer-facing production services with defined SLOs, including on-call programs, incident management, and operational excellence across teams of varying size and seniority
Demonstrated experience managing engineers across a range of seniority levels, including early-career engineers, with a track record of meaningful career growth outcomes
Experience owning cross-team platform relationships: managing inbound dependency requests, negotiating priorities, and communicating commitments with confidence
Track record of delivering complex, multi-quarter technical roadmaps — including large-scale migrations or legacy system consolidations — in fast-moving environments
Preferred
Experience with notification, messaging, or communications infrastructure at scale — email, SMS, push, or WhatsApp delivery.
Experience with customer journey orchestration, marketing automation, or lifecycle messaging platforms
Hands-on familiarity with agent frameworks and orchestration tooling (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, Autogen, Temporal, or similar) and practical knowledge of where these systems break down in production
Experience building end-to-end observability and business-impact alerting for multi-hop asynchronous pipelines
Experience managing teams that own 24/7 on-call rotations and production services with external SLAs or vendor dependencies

title: Principal Product Manager, Technical ES, Mission AI
description:
Some of the most consequential AI work in the country happens where the internet does not reach. As the Principal Product Manager for Mission AI, you will decide what that work becomes. You will own the product strategy for AI capability delivered on one of the largest AI infrastructure programs AWS has ever taken on: a dedicated, accredited GPU environment where strong open-weight and Amazon models are adapted to a national security customer's own data and problems.
There is no established product playbook for this. Public benchmarks, model hubs, and package repositories are not available inside the environment, compute is a fixed on-premises fleet, and the customer's mission needs are still being defined. You will work directly with the customer's technical leaders, analysts, and operators to find the problems worth solving, then turn them into clear requirements that scientists and engineers can build against. You will decide what ships first, what "better than the base model" has to mean before we claim it, and how capability moves from the lab to the people who rely on it. You will also set product direction for the program's infrastructure product manager, so platform and AI capability run as one roadmap.
You join at the start. The lab's first scientists are being hired now, and the decisions you make in your first year shape both what the program delivers and what it is asked to deliver next.
The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the product vision and multi-year roadmap for mission AI capability: adapted models, evaluation suites, and the inference and agentic services the customer's engineers integrate into their mission systems.
- Run discovery with customer technical leads, analysts, and operators to find and rank the highest-value mission use cases, and write the narratives (PR/FAQ, strategy documents) that drive investment decisions.
- Define what success means for each use case before work starts, partnering with the lab's science leads to set evaluation standards and the margin a model must clear to count as an improvement.
- Translate mission needs into functional and technical requirements, and make the trade-offs between capability, compute budget, schedule, and accreditation constraints.
- Own launch readiness inside the accredited environment: technical readiness, independent verification and validation, accreditation and authorization gates, operational handoff, and customer adoption.
- Shape future task orders: build the evidence-backed business case and scope for the next wave of mission AI work, partnering with program, contracts, and finance.
- Be accountable for outcomes: track adoption, mission impact, and delivery against goals, and report progress in program and executive reviews.
- Own customer engagement across the service lifecycle: adoption, optimization, problem resolution, and evolution of each capability once it is in mission use. Own escalations on the services you ship and dive deep with engineers to resolve them.
- Influence the engineering roadmaps of the customer's technical decision makers, so their mission systems are built to take advantage of what the lab delivers next.
- Write architecture and technical requirements documents for the lab's services, and contribute to engineering design reviews on how they are built, served, and scaled.
- Partner with Tech Business Development, Solutions Architects, ProServe, and engineering leaders inside and outside AWS to drive service success.
- Set product direction for and mentor the program's infrastructure product manager, and help hire and develop the product team as the program scales.
A day in the life
You start the morning reading the overnight evaluation results with the lab's scientists, checking whether an adapted model has cleared the bar you agreed with the customer for a priority mission task. Mid-morning, you work with customer analysts on a workflow they run every day, looking for the step where a model would change their outcome rather than just their speed. After lunch, you review the infrastructure team's serving plan and decide whether the next release can meet its accreditation gate on schedule or needs to be re-scoped. You close the day drafting the business case for a capability the customer has not asked for yet, but that the evidence says they will need in the next task order.
About the team
The Mission AI Model Lab is the science team behind AWS's Mission AI program. We take existing models and make them useful for problems that matter to national security, working on dedicated AI infrastructure built for exactly that. This lab is purpose-built and these are among its first scientists, so the people who join now help shape how it works and what it builds. We sit where frontier-model research meets national security delivery, and we value invention on genuinely new problems, evaluation we can defend, and plain talk with the people who rely on what we build.
Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

title: Principal TPM, AI Engineering, AI Engineering
description:
Software engineering is where AI is changing work fastest. Developers everywhere now use AI coding tools, but the organizational gains have not followed, and most enterprises have faster individual developers alongside the same delivery outcomes. AWS AI Engineering exists to close that gap. We help customers systematically build better software with AI across the whole software development lifecycle. AI-native development is now moving from early adopters into the enterprise, and the hard part is no longer proving that it works. It is making it scale.
We are looking for a Principal TPM to help shape how that happens. You will work alongside our engineering teams to bring direction together from two streams of signal: what we learn inside customers' engineering organizations, and where the industry is heading. Customer signal tells you what hurts today. Industry signal tells you what will be table stakes in six months. Connecting the two into a point of view the team can act on, and keeping it current as both move, is the center of this role.
Our current work includes an open-source, AI-native development lifecycle we created and continue to evolve with customers, along with offerings that give AI agents a deep understanding of large codebases and move customers toward autonomous software delivery. Those offerings will keep changing as the technology does, and the charter behind them will not.
Key job responsibilities
Bring the direction together
Work with our engineering teams to connect customer signal and industry signal into a clear direction for how AWS helps customers become AI-native across the software development lifecycle. Find where teams are solving the same problem in parallel and bring that work together, so the organization makes one piece of real progress rather than three partial ones. Help sequence work against customer readiness and keep the portfolio coherent as individual offerings come and go.
Define the methodology, then make it adoptable
Drive the definition, standardization, and adoption of our AI-native development lifecycle as something customers can run themselves. Build consensus on the practices and standards that make it real, and replace fragmented experimentation with a credible default path that fits each customer's risk tolerance.
Own adoption, and scale it
Treat adoption as the deliverable rather than the follow-up, through enablement, documentation, reference implementations, assessments, and self-service paths that carry customers from first experiment to production-scale practice. Design the mechanisms that convert individual developer adoption into enterprise standardization and that let the wider AWS field carry this work without you in the room. Account for organizations whose constraints differ from the ones you designed for, and for the long tail where adoption usually stalls.
Define how success is measured, and hold us to it
Define and track outcome-based KPIs for the charter, including adoption and depth of use inside customer organizations, persistence of changed behavior long after the engagement, and improvements in delivery speed, quality, and the economics of building software. Insist on rigorous evaluation of the offerings we build, the agents inside them, and our own claims about what works. Build measurement frameworks customers can run on themselves, and recommend stopping work that is not paying off.
Build leverage out of engagements
Turn lessons from individual customer engagements into repeatable patterns and scalable assets. Productize what was built for one customer when it has broader value, and resist treating every new request as bespoke. Represent the voice of the customer internally, translating patterns and adoption blockers into actionable input for AWS service teams so that what we learn in the field shapes the products customers build on.
Lead across the organization and with customers
Influence without relying on authority, aligning engineering, field, and regional teams worldwide on shared direction and sequencing. Act as a trusted advisor to customer executives and practitioners, solving the business problem rather than only the technical one and investing in the long-term relationship over the one-off win. Build the playbook and enablement that lets the wider AWS field carry this work, and represent it externally through open source, conference talks, and technical writing.
A day in the life
You split your time between setting direction and staying close to the work. On one day you might sit with a customer's engineering team to understand why they abandoned part of the lifecycle after week three, then meet a CTO to agree what success looks like for a 15,000 developer organization. On another you might review adoption data across regions to decide where the next investment goes, work out what a stalled rollout actually needs, or turn a pattern that worked for one customer into something the whole field can run. You make calls with incomplete information, hold direction under pressure, and change course when the evidence warrants.
