- 10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of software development experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Preferred qualifications: - 8+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience

title: Principal Technical Program Manager, PXT Central Science

This is a technical program role that demands technical depth in science and software engineering. You will bring strong, data-driven judgment about the statistical systems that power employee listening, using that judgment to frame trade-offs, sequence delivery, and keep significantly complex scientific programs on track across teams.
As our senior technical program leader, you will operate with complete independence across the Corporate, Worldwide Operations, and cross-cutting portfolios. You will drive program delivery where the business and methodological strategy has not yet been defined — working from research questions and methodology owned by science leadership, and orchestrating the science, engineering, and business teams required to deliver them at scale. title: Senior Product Manager Tech - Business Process Architecture, Amazon LEO
description:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we've designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Product Manager Tech – Business Process Architecture to serve as the single-threaded owner of Amazon Leo's enterprise process architecture. Acting as a strategic orchestrator, you will define how Leo's manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and operational processes move from their current "as-is" state to a deliberately designed, governed, and measurable "to-be" state. You will own the enterprise process methodology toolbox and apply the right method to each problem rather than forcing a single framework, using process mining, simulation, and data-driven discovery to replace opinion with objective insight.
This role spans the full enterprise process-architecture competency set. On the transformational side, you will build the business case and vision, communicate it, and lead the organizational change required to make process transformation stick. On the operational side, you will discover formal and informal processes, model and analyze them, design improved target states, and establish the governance model, process policies, and performance management that link process inputs and outputs to business outcomes. On the technical side, you will translate target processes into solution architecture, applying agile and model-driven delivery and designing for usability — realizing business goals through a clear understanding of the business, information, and technical architectures.
You will be the connective tissue across Leo's enterprise application landscape, with a deep focus on ERP (SAP S/4HANA) and PLM (Teamcenter) and their integration with the broader estate — MES, supply chain planning, and quality systems. You will define integration and data-flow patterns, protect master-data integrity across the digital thread, and ensure that process designs are feasible, adoptable, and durable before resources are committed.
Key job responsibilities

- Author OP1/OP2 narratives.
- Apply project management principles to drive transformation, balancing constraints against desired outcomes.
- Communicate transformation goals, benefits, and successes to gain stakeholder support, and apply change management to overcome resistance to process change.
- Lead business process discovery to identify formal and informal processes and understand the "as-is" state.
- Model, analyze, and design processes — visually depicting them to assess impact and design improved "to-be" states.

- Deliver solution architecture and design across ERP (SAP S/4HANA), PLM (Teamcenter), and the broader enterprise estate — realizing business goals through business, information, and technical architectures.

- Apply process optimization and simulation to test the impact of changes before implementation.
- Analyze user interactions with processes to improve usability.

title: Sr. Product Manager - Tech, OpsTech Solutions, OTS Delivery Software Engineering (DSE)
description:
Every Amazon package that ships, every grocery order that is fulfilled, and every associate who needs IT help depends on technology our teams keep running. Amazon's OpsTech Solutions (OTS) is the IT operations and infrastructure organization for all of Amazon Worldwide Operations, including Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), delivering reliable technology to more than one million associates and operators across every geography. OTS is transforming from reactive support to proactive, prescriptive, AI-powered service delivery, and ServiceNow is the platform where that work happens.
What this role is: You will own the product strategy for the OTS Incident Management Platform (ITSM), the core system of record and orchestration layer for how the organization receives, records, routes, and resolves work. Every requester contact, Service Desk interaction, and Field IT task flows through the incident record you own. You decide what gets built, what gets retired, and how ITSM becomes the foundation that the rest of the OTS product portfolio plugs into.
Our team is organized around three questions that apply to every persona we serve: How does someone ask for help? How does the organization receive and organize that work? How does the work get resolved? This role owns the center of that model. Your peers own the requester front door (OneSupportHub and Virtual Agent), Service Desk Workforce Optimization, AI resolution intelligence (OTS Assist and PathFinder), and Field IT productivity. ITSM is where all of those come together on a single record, so the decisions you make shape how well every adjacent product works.
The opportunity is to move ITSM from a place where fulfillers log work to a platform that actively guides it. Today, Service Desk fulfillers and Field IT technicians lose time to platform friction and assemble each resolution themselves from memory and scattered knowledge. You will turn ITSM into the orchestrator that brings AI-generated resolution plans, validated data, and trusted knowledge into the fulfiller's workflow, so the right next step is the obvious one. Your customers are Service Desk fulfillers, Field IT technicians and managers, knowledge authors, and the engineers who integrate other services with the incident record.
Key Highlights
• Own the product strategy and roadmap for the OTS Incident Management Platform (ITSM), the system of record and orchestration layer for OTS work.
• Drive the reactive-to-prescriptive transformation by making ITSM the place where AI-generated resolution plans become the default way to work an incident.
• Lead Knowledge Base improvements so content is easy to find, trustworthy, and measured.
• Work at the center of a product team whose adjacent products (intake, routing, workforce optimization, AI resolution) all depend on your platform.
Key job responsibilities
- Define and own a multi-year product vision and roadmap for ITSM, covering incident and task management, orchestration and validation, ITSM user experience, and Knowledge Management.
- Act as the voice of the customer for Service Desk and Field IT, using shadowing, feedback, and operational data to translate real workflow friction into prioritized requirements.
- Partner with the AI resolution product team to deliver prescriptive, guided resolution on the incident record, and own the fulfiller-facing experience and its adoption.
- Set clear ownership boundaries and integration contracts between ITSM and adjacent products (intake, routing, workforce optimization, AI agents) so teams build on the platform rather than around it.
- Partner with engineering leaders to shape platform architecture, drive build-vs-configure-vs-buy decisions on ServiceNow, and manage platform health and technical debt.
- Establish north-star and adoption metrics for the platform (e.g., handle time, resolution-plan adoption, documentation quality, knowledge reuse) and report on them through Monthly and Quarterly Business Reviews.
- Contribute to annual planning mechanisms (OP1/OP2) with clear, well-reasoned investment proposals, and maintain mechanisms to continuously capture voice of the customer.
A day in the life
Your day moves between the floor and the roadmap. You might start by shadowing IT technicians to see where a knowledge article pulls them off a ticket or where a chat times out mid-conversation, then turn those observations into user stories with your engineering partners. Midday, you join an architecture discussion on how AI-generated resolution plans write back to the incident record and where that boundary sits with the AI team. In the afternoon, you review adoption metrics, make prioritization trade-offs with stakeholders across the IT organization, and draft a strategy narrative or OP2 investment proposal for senior review.
About the team
The ServiceNow Product Management team builds the products that are the backbone of OTS operations. Amazon employees, Service Desk agents, and Field IT technicians rely on these ServiceNow experiences to complete their work every day. The team is a group of Product Managers, each owning one clear product space so they can go deep instead of switching between unrelated problems, supported by a dedicated UX designer. Your engineering counterparts sit within the same larger organization, and your primary stakeholders are the Service Desk and Field IT organizations.

title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Network Product Development, Interconnects
description:
AWS builds one of the largest networks in the world, and every rack that lands in a data center depends on optics, copper, fiber and switches all arriving on time. The Network Product Development (NPD) Interconnects team designs and brings to production the optical modules, DAC/AEC copper cables and structured fiber that connect AWS infrastructure.
We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to help drive how our products move from forecast to factory to data center. You will be the day-to-day interface between Supply Chain, our manufacturing vendors and the NPD engineers who design our products. You make sure each group has the technical context, data and decisions it needs from the others. When a forecast changes, a supplier raises a constraint or a build stalls, you bring the right people together quickly, frame the trade-offs clearly and drive the issue to resolution.
We work quickly and practically. Rather than waiting for large software programs, you will use AI tools, agents, scripts and lightweight workflows to stand up working processes fast. You'll run them on a regular cadence with our partners and improve them as you learn. Once a process has proven itself, you will help turn it into durable tooling.
Key job responsibilities
- Drive the end-to-end program for interconnect products (optical modules, DAC/AEC, fiber and structured cabling) from forecast to delivery, and report progress and risks to NPD and Networking leadership through a regular business review.
- Act as the primary interface between Supply Chain, vendors and NPD engineering. Translate engineering constraints into supply implications and supply constraints into engineering decisions.
- Coordinate technical review of significant forecast changes (product mix or volume) with engineering and Supply Chain before they are shared with suppliers.
- Help keep long-range capacity commitments and short-range build signals distinct. Raise it early when an execution signal risks undoing a long-lead commitment (DSPs, lasers, PCBs, raw fiber materials, line capacity).
- Partner with engineering and Supply Chain to keep BOM and allocation data consistent, so sub-tier requirements line up across commodity managers.
- Run scenario analyses (for example a 50% demand increase or decrease) with Supply Chain and engineering to show where commitments break across components and sub-tiers, and help teams agree on the response.
- Work with vendors and Supply Chain to track supplier commitments and de-commitments for critical sub-tier parts
- Drive a weekly clear-to-build (CTB) review with vendors and Supply Chain that combines component availability against the build plan, escalates shortfalls early and handles excess inventory without stopping the line.
- Track capacity KPIs with our vendors. Work with engineering and site teams to validate capacity constraints when the data doesn't line up.
- Coordinate with Supply Chain and deployment teams on inventory at VMI hubs and rack integrators, so production plans reflect where finished units can actually go.
- Support rack integration improvements with engineering and integrators: rack portfolio standardization, production-readiness validation for new rack designs, first-pass yield, test time and the time from PO to start of assembly.
- Use AI tools and agents every day to automate data gathering, reconcile vendor and Supply Chain data, generate status reports and catch issues early.
- Build AI-assisted workflows that cut manual spreadsheet work for engineers and Supply Chain partners, and share what works across the team.
- Write requirements and work with software teams to turn proven processes and AI-assisted workflows into durable tools.
A day in the life
Your week might start with a CTB review across optics and fiber vendors, where an AI agent you set up has already reconciled the latest vendor data and flagged a laser shortfall weeks ahead. You then pull Supply Chain and engineering together to work through what a forecast revision means for supplier agreements. Later you follow up with a vendor on a capacity constraint that doesn't match their reported output, and join a call with a rack integrator on why a high-volume configuration keeps failing first-pass test. You write clear updates for leadership and turn this week's manual fixes into next week's automated workflow. Expect regular travel between Seattle and the Bay Area, as well as to supplier and integrator sites, mostly in Asia.
About the team
NPD Interconnects handles product development for the optics, copper and fiber that link AWS networks, from early engineering through NPI and volume production. We work closely with the NPD switch and software teams, Global Supply Management, fabric and deployment teams, and our manufacturing partners worldwide. We value strong partnerships, mechanisms over good intentions, and a "trust, but verify" approach to the data we rely on.

title: AI Research Scientist: Multimodal Foundation Models - Architecture, Pre-Training & Distillation
description:
The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem.
Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment.
You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. Where appropriate, this work may also lead to publications and the open sourcing of selected models, research artifacts, evaluations, or tools.
In this role, you will investigate fundamental questions about how multimodal foundation models should be designed, trained, and distilled.
You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. Your work will explore how capabilities developed in large foundation models can be effectively transferred to smaller, more efficient models without treating distillation as an isolated downstream step.
A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. This includes designing architectures that distill effectively, studying how teacher and student models should be trained together, and developing distillation methods that preserve reasoning, multimodal understanding, instruction following, and other important capabilities under constrained model capacity.
Rather than treating deployment constraints as an afterthought, you will incorporate them into the research process—from early architecture experiments and pre-training through distillation and final model evaluation.
You may thrive in this role if you:
* Want to invent new foundation-model architectures rather than only adapt existing models.
* Enjoy combining scientific ambition with real compute, memory, latency, and energy constraints.
* Believe that small and efficient models can be a frontier research problem, not merely a compression exercise.
* Are comfortable working across model research, data, systems, and hardware boundaries.
* Care about translating research into private, useful, and deeply integrated intelligent experiences.
* Want your work to have both product impact and a presence in the broader research community.
Potential research directions include:
* Novel dense, recurrent, state-space, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid foundation-model architectures.
* Multimodal pre-training across language, images, video, audio, and sensor-derived representations.
* Compute-optimal model and data scaling, including data mixtures, curricula, tokenization, and training objectives.
* Architecture and algorithm co-design for memory-efficient and energy-efficient inference on Apple silicon.
* Offline and on-policy distillation using teacher-generated data, logits, representations, rationales, and other supervision signals.
Minimum qualifications: Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and running large-scale pre-training experiments for large language models.
Experience with LLM pre-training topics such as model architecture, training objectives, data mixtures, tokenization, curricula, scaling, and optimization.
Strong proficiency with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and distributed training systems.
Experience evaluating pre-trained models across language understanding, reasoning, instruction following, or multimodal capabilities.
Strong understanding of transformer-based architectures and current approaches to efficient or scalable foundation-model training.
Master’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in machine learning, computer science, or a related technical field, and a minimum of 6 years relevant experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience contributing to major foundation-model pre-training efforts or leading architecture experiments that influenced a large training run.
Research contributions in model architecture, scaling laws, multimodal pre-training, optimization, efficient attention, mixture-of-experts, state-space models, or related areas.
Experience with knowledge distillation, including offline or off-policy distillation, on-policy distillation, self-distillation, sequence-level distillation, logic matching, or representation transfer.
Experience designing teacher–student training pipelines or transferring capabilities from large foundation models to smaller models.
Experience with multimodal models spanning language, vision, video, audio, or other sensor modalities.
Understanding of inference efficiency, memory hierarchy, hardware accelerators, or hardware–software co-design.
Strong publication record, influential open-source contributions, or an equivalent record of applied research impact

title: AI Software Engineer - Calendar Intelligence
description:
Apple has changed how people live, connect, and work, and the Calendar team wants to rethink what a calendar can do for the people using it. A calendar knows when someone is busy. It knows very little about which of those commitments matter, which ones could move, or when would be a good time for something new. We're looking for an engineer to help answer those questions, on device and privately, for billions of people. The right person has strong machine learning foundations and is just as comfortable writing the software that ships a model as building the model itself. You'll help take ideas from a single sentence to a shipped feature, and you'll bring the evaluation that tells us whether it works.
In this role you'll drive the modeling and evaluation behind intelligence features in Calendar, from the first framing through launch, as part of a very collaborative team. A request will often start as one line, and you'll work with the team to turn it into a problem we can solve: what signal exists, what a good answer looks like, which approach fits, and how we'll know it's right. You'll design the evaluation before you build the model. That means the metrics, the eval sets, the baselines a model has to beat, and human review for the places where a metric can't tell you enough.
You won't always have good data, so part of the job is finding it and getting something useful out of it when there isn't much. You'll need to get real statistical strength out of priors, shared structure, and self-supervision. You'll also work with a range of large language models, on device and on server, deciding where a model call earns its cost, where a smaller model trained on a larger model's judgments does better, and where a well-tuned heuristic beats both.
You'll join a small team of senior systems engineers who ship this work across Apple's platforms, several of them with deep backgrounds in ML data engineering. There's no hard line between roles, so you'll write production code alongside them in whatever part of the stack the problem needs. Calendar also builds on signals and models from other ML teams across Apple, and a lot of this role is working with them: building on what they have, agreeing on shared interfaces, and recognizing when we need our own. You'll work closely with design and product as well. We need someone who writes clearly, can explain a model's tradeoffs to engineers who aren't ML specialists, and is comfortable driving a problem forward before the path is defined.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, EE, Applied Mathematics, or related field with 2+ years experience in developing ML / AI driven software.
Proficiency in one or more of the following programming languages: Python, Swift, Objective-C, or C++
Experience developing software prototypes and features driven by Large Language Models and designing tool and function-calling interfaces, constructing context, and validating model output
Fluency with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, with good judgment about where to apply them and how to verify what they produce.
Experience driving an ambiguous problem with cross-functional partners, including other ML teams, from a loose idea through launch, and getting alignment on shared interfaces along the way.
Exceptional problem-solving skills, and the ability to drive alignment across teams on shared API surfaces
Preferred qualifications: Experience designing and developing systems that are efficient in resource constrained environments — latency, memory, and power budgets on device
Solid foundation in machine learning, probability, and statistics, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models in a framework such as PyTorch or JAX
A track record of designing the evaluation for what you ship: metrics, held-out sets, baselines, and noticing when a metric has stopped measuring what you care about
Proven ability to excel in a fast-paced development team

You will provide critical technical direction for dataset design and safety alignment strategies, while directly overseeing the implementation of end-to-end mitigation architectures in production. Pre and Post-launch, you will remain hands-on—analyzing evaluation results, conducting failure investigations, and leveraging human and automated feedback to continuously improve feature safety and build user trust. description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. This position requires a highly motivated person who wants to help us bridge the gap between research advances and practical applications in generative AI and multimodal foundation models. In addition, you will have an opportunity to engage and collaborate with several teams across Apple to deliver the best products.

Proficiency in Python and in a modern deep learning framework such as PyTorch or JAX.
Experience with rapid prototyping, reproduction, and validation of research ideas.
Master's or equivalent practical experience, in Computer Science, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, or related technical field.

title: Compute Runtime Software Engineer
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center and Apple platforms — with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source project bringing native container support to macOS desktops.
We're looking to add talented, passionate seasoned domain experts who love hard systems problems and want to build foundational technology used across Apple and the open source community, ready to take ownership of significant technologies.

Much of this work is greenfield, solving problems unique to running on Apple's own hardware in the data center, at a scale and with constraints the rest of the industry hasn't had to solve for. Beyond the datacenter, we maintain Apple Container, our open source desktop tooling that lets developers around the world run containers natively on macOS.
We're looking for a domain expert with depth across multiple technical areas, someone used to designing major features and resolving highly complex, ambiguous problems creatively — taking ownership of significant technologies to drive real impact across the organization, ready to take risks, course-correct quickly, and drive ideas from inception to implementation, building a reputation as someone the broader org seeks out for technical direction and standards, and to actively mentor engineers at all levels.

title: Machine Learning Researcher: Agentic Post-Training for On-Device Models
description:
The Video Computer Vision (VCV) organization is an applied research and engineering team developing next-generation multimodal intelligence technologies across Apple products. Within VCV, our team builds intelligent systems that combine multimodal understanding, reasoning, and tool use to deliver compelling user experiences. Our work is deeply integrated into the Apple ecosystem, partnering across hardware, software, and ML teams to deliver real-time, scalable, and privacy-preserving experiences reaching millions of users.
In this role, you will develop post-training methods that turn foundation models into capable, reliable, and efficient agents for on-device execution. You will develop supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning methods for agentic models, alongside the training data, interactive environments, reward signals, and evaluations needed to advance reasoning, tool use, and long-horizon tasks. A central research challenge is enabling smaller models to make effective decisions and complete multi-step tasks within tight latency, memory, and energy budgets. You will investigate how to improve reasoning, planning, and tool use while reducing reliance on lengthy generated reasoning and large inference budgets. Research directions may include structured reasoning, adaptive computation, and training objectives that balance task success with computational cost. You will own the projects end to end: identify capability gaps, formulate hypotheses, build training pipelines, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate frontier research into Apple products that deliver meaningful value to users.

Strong programming skills in Python and proficiency with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
Demonstrated ability to formulate research hypotheses, implement training and evaluation pipelines, conduct controlled experiments, and draw well-supported conclusions.
Preferred qualifications: PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, Natural Language Processing, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Research focus on foundation models, reinforcement learning, agentic systems, multimodal reasoning, or efficient machine learning.

Experience developing or training agents for tool use and long-horizon tasks.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Platform Engineer), G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE)
description:
G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE) is IS&T's dedicated technology partner for Apple's general and administrative functions — including people, finance, facilities, legal, and security. The team builds and delivers integrated technology solutions that keep these functions running efficiently and securely at global scale. GSE also works closely with business teams to develop custom tools that improve productivity and bring greater automation and consistency to G&A operations across Apple.
When you engineer for People Systems, your users are Apple’s most vital asset: its People. We are seeking a Senior Platform Engineer to shape the technical strategy for People Systems with a passion for platforms where configuration is the product, and agentic workflows that redefine what's possible.
You will be working on a Platform that helps define features. Data models, rules, workflows, permissions, screens and reports are all versioned configuration, interpreted at runtime, so the people closest to a problem can change how the system behaves without waiting for a release. Hundreds of components must behave as one system. We are looking for a passionate engineer who can make that true.
We value engineers who bring both technical excellence and product thinking. You'll make the architectural calls that balance fast delivery against long-term platform health, and build systems that are scalable, secure and resilient by design rather than by retrofit.
This role requires someone who thrives on complexity but ships simplicity.
Collaboration is central to how we work. You’ll partner with product managers and cross-functional engineering teams to understand problems deeply before reaching for solutions. The best engineers here are the ones who ask “why” before “how.” If you care deeply about precision, data integrity, and crafting platforms where scale meets human empathy, come join us to do the best work of your life.
Minimum qualifications: 8 years proven experience developing software in a professional capacity. Longer experience strongly preferred.
6 years proven experience with Java or Kotlin, including mastery in concurrency, memory management, and performance optimization techniques.
8 years proven mastery in OOP principles, data structures, algorithms, and software design patterns (e.g. GoF), with a proven focus on implementing testable, maintainable, and extensible backend code.
6 years proven experience in least one modern frontend stack (such as React/Next.js) coupled with LLM feature development, utilizing the top 3 ecosystem languages: TypeScript, Python, and JavaScript.
B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional work experience.
Preferred qualifications: Track record of leading software projects that span multiple, distributed teams as a tech lead (TL), while mentoring senior-level software engineers.
Hands-on experience leveraging GenAI coding tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot, Codex) to accelerate the software development lifecycle, enhance code quality, and streamline debugging and testing processes.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Ads
description:
Apple is where we use the power of technology to enrich people's lives. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other's ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It's the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you'll do more than join something — you'll add something.
Join the Apple Ads Engineering team and help build an advertising platform that benefits both customers and advertisers. Our technology makes advertising possible on the App Store, Apple News, Stocks, and Apple TV — helping people discover content, supporting creators and publishers, and connecting advertisers of all sizes with engaged audiences, all with the unwavering commitment to privacy you expect from Apple. In this role, you will design, develop, and launch the highly-performant, internet-scale backend systems that select and deliver the right ads in real time, collaborating across engineering, product, and infrastructure to bring elegant solutions into production at Apple scale.
You will design, develop, and operate the distributed services that make real-time ad selection possible at Apple. You will architect and build low-latency, high-availability, high-throughput ad-serving systems in a cloud environment, engineer secure and scalable data processing pipelines that operate on petabyte-scale datasets, and implement performant services that handle very high data volumes and QPS. You will work cross-functionally to ensure that optimal and correct ads are available for real-time selection, and that observability and flexibility are provided for stakeholders. While this role focuses on the candidate retrieval part of Apple Ads, we are not constrained by organization structure and offer the flexibility to contribute across a variety of backend systems, including opportunities to apply algorithmic search, machine learning, NLP, and AI to hard retrieval problems. You will write clean, efficient, well-documented code, participate in code reviews, and mentor other engineers on the team. Collaboration with internal partners across indexing, search, serving, operations, and program management to define requirements and deliver high-quality solutions is essential. You should be passionate about building products that protect user privacy and thrive in a fast-paced environment with rapidly changing priorities — and have fun doing it.
Minimum qualifications: 6+ years of industry experience architecting and developing internet-scale server software for Linux systems, including scalable micro-services or data-driven platforms.
Strong background in computer science fundamentals, including algorithms and data structures.
Strong coding skills in Go, Java, Rust, C++, Scala, or a similar OOP/Functional language.
Hands-on experience designing and operating scalable micro-services.
Experience with search technologies such as Lucene, Solr, or Elasticsearch. Expertise with NoSQL datastores (e.g., Cassandra).
Proficiency with data processing technologies (e.g., Kafka, Spark, Flink) and methods for processing petabyte-scale datasets.
Experience with AWS services such as Amazon S3, EC2, and EKS/Kubernetes. Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
Demonstrated ability to work on complex problems and systems, alone or as part of a team, to deliver complete systems end to end.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical cross-functional teams, including operations and project management partners.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
Experience creating groundbreaking technology for algorithmic search, machine learning, natural language processing, and artificial intelligence.
Experience building ad-serving, recommendation, or large-scale retrieval systems.
Familiarity with real-time bidding, candidate retrieval, or ranking pipelines.
Experience operating services with strict latency and availability SLOs.
Familiarity with privacy-preserving system design and data-handling practices.
Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals — consensus, replication, and fault tolerance.
A desire to work in a fast-paced and challenging environment, and a fast learner with strong motivation for growing and learning new technologies.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Card & Savings
description:
The Apple Card & Savings team is building the financial products that put users in control of their money. We built Apple Card to reinvent how credit cards work, and we continue to launch groundbreaking features used by millions of people every day. We are looking for an experienced engineer who loves owning critical services end to end, takes pride in operational excellence, and thrives in a highly regulated environment where correctness, reliability, and compliance requirements shape every technical decision.
You'll design, build, test, deliver, and operate the distributed services that power Apple Card and Savings — from applications, accounts, and transactions to payments, savings transfers, rewards, and customer notifications. You'll be given the support of a talented team, access to modern technologies, and the autonomy to take full ownership of your work.
Our team operates as DevOps: we build what we run. You'll be hands-on in every phase of the lifecycle — shipping changes safely through automated pipelines and controlled rollouts, participating in an on-call rotation, joining incident response and post-incident reviews, and automating away operational toil. You'll build reliable integrations with financial institution and payment network partners and with other Apple services such as Wallet, Apple Cash, and iCloud.
As an experienced member of the team, you'll own features from specification through production, review code, contribute to technical design, write clear documentation, and help onboard and mentor teammates. Success in this role requires self-motivation, clear communication, a collaborative approach, and a commitment to engineering excellence and continuous improvement.

Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals, including idempotency, retries, timeouts, and consistency trade-offs.
Proficiency in a modern backend programming language (e.g. Kotlin, Java).
Experience debugging production issues using logs, metrics, and traces, and following through on fixes and post-incident improvements.
A testing-first mindset: experience writing thorough unit and integration tests as a natural part of development, and designing code with testability in mind.
Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical issues to non-engineering stakeholders and external partners.

Experience using generative AI tools throughout the software development lifecycle to produce high-quality software.

Experience with CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and safe release practices (e.g. canary deployments, feature flags, automated rollback).
Experience with observability tools (e.g. Datadog, Splunk, OpenTelemetry), service level objectives (SLOs), and building actionable alerts that detect issues before customers or partners do.
Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging (e.g. Kafka or equivalent event streaming) and with SQL/NoSQL databases at scale (e.g. Aurora, DynamoDB).
Understanding of security and privacy fundamentals for protecting sensitive customer and financial data (e.g. mTLS, PKI and certificate lifecycle management, JWT).

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Services Engineering
description:
The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).
Deep, demonstrated experience in one of the following, and working fluency in the other: Operating live migration, live patching, or kexec-style host updates across a production fleet, including the failures: non-convergence, aborts and rollback, and fleet-wide rollout safety. Building live migration, snapshot/restore, or device-state serialization inside a hypervisor or VMM (for example QEMU/KVM, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Xen, or Hyper-V).
Advanced programming language proficiency in C, C++, Rust, Swift or Go, with a track record of designing and developing high performance, secured, scalable and reliable systems.
Track record of owning technical design end-to-end, from design docs and architecture tradeoffs through implementation and review.
Experience setting technical direction for a group of engineers, with or without formal management responsibility.
Preferred qualifications: Experience with Linux kernel and system programming (KVM, userfaultfd, VFIO, kexec, kernel live patching).
Understanding of dirty-page tracking, memory and device state handling, and time and CPU-model compatibility across hosts.
Experience with live migration of devices that carry hardware state (VFIO, vDPA, SR-IOV).
Experience designing benchmarks and load tests to characterize downtime and performance impact during an upgrade.
Experience contributing to or maintaining open source virtualization projects (Cloud Hypervisor, rust-vmm, QEMU, KVM).
Experience with Kubernetes node lifecycle, draining, and fleet rollout orchestration.
Experience building a new team from zero, including hiring.

title: Sensing Product Design Architecture Engineer
description:
In our fast-paced, device centric world, Apple is constantly innovating to meet the ever growing demand for cutting-edge features. We’re seeking a talented engineer to join our Sensing Product Design Architecture team and help us set the standard for excellence, creativity, and innovation. You will leverage advanced analytical and numerical methods to develop robust, data-driven design solutions for some of Apple's most challenging and cutting-edge features, ultimately deﬁning the foundational performance of products used by millions worldwide.

You will work with a talented multifunctional team to generate design concepts and quantify performance impacts through complex analytical models for various sensing technologies within Apple’s portfolio of products.

BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field
Deep understanding of advanced mechanical engineering principles (solid mechanics, materials science, heat transfer).
Proven experience with data-driven design using statistical analysis (e.g., Monte Carlo, DoE) and tolerance analysis.
Experience designing for a high-volume production environment; consumer electronics or sensing is a plus.
Preferred qualifications: Expert proﬁciency in 3D CAD software (e.g., Siemens NX, SolidWorks, Creo) for the creation, modiﬁcation, and preparation of mechanical designs speciﬁcally for advanced analytical modeling and simulation workﬂows.
Demonstrated mastery in advanced computational mechanics, including Finite Element Analysis (FEA), to model and predict complex multi-physics behaviors (e.g., structural, thermal, vibrational, fatigue) critical to the performance and reliability of sensing modules.
Expertise in analytical programming languages such as Python or Matlab for advanced data analysis, scientiﬁc computing, numerical simulations, and workﬂow automation. Experience developing and deploying scalable analytical tools or web applications to empower broader engineering teams is a signiﬁcant advantage.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex technical ﬁndings for diverse audiences, drive cross-functional alignment, and positively contribute to the engineering community through technical leadership and mentorship.

As a member of a fast-paced team, you have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of people every day.

Strong C++ skills, including modern C++
Experience breaking down large problems and delivering robust solutions
Curiosity about new technologies and flexibility to work across different layers of the software stack

Proven track record of shipping products or contributing to open-source projects
Experience deploying algorithms to GPUs or other hardware accelerators
Strong engineering rigor, communication, and collaboration skills
Excellent problem-solving and analytical abilities

title: Software Engineer – Digital Asset Management, Retail & Marcom Engineering
description:
At Apple, we strive every single day to craft products and platforms that enrich people’s lives. Our successes are the result of skilled domain experts working in an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and rethinking old problems in new ways.

The team owns the technology behind both Apple's online and physical stores and drives the interactive marketing experiences and tools that keep creative operations moving. Together, those functions deliver the technology behind every product story Apple tells and every purchase a customer makes.
As a member of the Digital Asset Management (DAM) Engineering team, you will design and develop next-generation enterprise asset platforms that manage, transform, index, and distribute massive volumes of creative and digital assets worldwide. You will sit at the intersection of enterprise software engineering, machine learning, and generative AI—infusing intelligent search, semantic understanding, auto-tagging, multimodal indexing, and AI-driven automation into foundational asset workflows. You will have the unique and rewarding opportunity to shape high-scale, mission-critical systems relied upon daily by cross-functional teams across Apple.
Our team is looking for a passionate, technically skilled software engineer who thrives in designing scalable distributed backend systems and integrating cutting-edge machine learning and generative AI capabilities. You will work autonomously within a collaborative team, partnering closely with product managers, ML practitioners, platform architects, and downstream engineering teams. We rely on your technical leadership and hands-on expertise to design resilient architectures, evolve enterprise DAM platforms, and implement robust AI/ML pipelines that deliver high impact.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related technical field, or
equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of professional software engineering experience with a strong focus on backend
systems.
Strong proficiency in Java (including modern Java features, concurrency, performance profiling,
and frameworks such as Spring Boot).
Practical experience designing and operating RESTful APIs, event-driven architectures, or

Distributed Storage & Media Processing: Familiarity with cloud object storage (S3), content
delivery networks (CDNs), and media processing pipelines.
DevOps & Cloud-Native Tooling: Working familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-
code, and production telemetry (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana).
Strong analytical problem-solving skills, with enthusiasm to tackle ambiguous technical
challenges in a fast-paced environment.

description:
At Apple, we focus deeply on our customers’ experience. Apple Ads brings this same approach to advertising, helping people find exactly what they’re looking for and helping advertisers grow their businesses. Strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented design
Strong proficiency in at least one object-oriented programming language (e.g., Java, C++, or equivalent)

title: Software Engineer, Apple Ads
description:
Apple is where we use the power of technology to enrich people's lives. Every new product we build, service we create, or Apple Store experience we deliver is the result of us making each other's ideas stronger. That happens because every one of us shares a belief that we can make something wonderful and share it with the world, changing lives for the better. It's the diversity of our people and their thinking that inspires the innovation that runs through everything we do. When we bring everybody in, we can do the best work of our lives. Here, you'll do more than join something — you'll add something.
Join the Apple Ads Engineering team and help build an advertising platform that benefits both customers and advertisers. Our technology makes advertising possible on the App Store, Apple News, Stocks, and Apple TV — helping people discover content, supporting creators and publishers, and connecting advertisers of all sizes with engaged audiences, all with the unwavering commitment to privacy you expect from Apple. In this role, you will design, develop, and launch the highly-performant, internet-scale backend systems that select and deliver the right ads in real time, collaborating across engineering, product, and infrastructure to bring elegant solutions into production at Apple scale.
You will design, develop, and operate the distributed services that make real-time ad selection possible at Apple. You will architect and build low-latency, high-availability, high-throughput ad-serving systems in a cloud environment, engineer secure and scalable data processing pipelines that operate on petabyte-scale datasets, and implement performant services that handle very high data volumes and QPS. While this role focuses on the candidate retrieval part of Apple Ads, we are not constrained by organization structure and offer the flexibility to contribute across a variety of backend systems, including opportunities to apply algorithmic search, machine learning, NLP, and AI to hard retrieval problems. You will write clean, efficient, well-documented code, participate in code reviews, and mentor other engineers on the team. You should be passionate about building products that protect user privacy and thrive in a fast-paced environment with rapidly changing priorities — and have fun doing it.
Minimum qualifications: 3+ years of industry experience architecting and developing internet-scale server software for Linux systems, including scalable micro-services or data-driven platforms.
Strong background in computer science fundamentals, including algorithms and data structures.
Strong coding skills in Go, Java, Rust, C++, Scala, or a similar OOP/Functional language.
Hands-on experience designing and operating scalable micro-services.
Experience with search technologies such as Lucene, Solr, or Elasticsearch. Expertise with NoSQL datastores (e.g., Cassandra).
Proficiency with data processing technologies (e.g., Kafka, Spark, Flink) and methods for processing petabyte-scale datasets.
Experience with AWS services such as Amazon S3, EC2, and EKS/Kubernetes. Strong problem-solving and debugging skills.
Demonstrated ability to work on complex problems and systems, alone or as part of a team, to deliver complete systems end to end.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical cross-functional teams, including operations and project management partners.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience.
Preferred qualifications: Experience creating groundbreaking technology for algorithmic search, machine learning, natural language processing, and artificial intelligence.
Experience building ad-serving, recommendation, or large-scale retrieval systems.
Familiarity with real-time bidding, candidate retrieval, or ranking pipelines.
Experience operating services with strict latency and availability SLOs.
Familiarity with privacy-preserving system design and data-handling practices.
Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals — consensus, replication, and fault tolerance.
A desire to work in a fast-paced and challenging environment, and a fast learner with strong motivation for growing and learning new technologies.

title: Software Engineer, Applied ML
description:
Our mission is to personalize the Apple user experience based on where you go, when you’re there, and what those places mean to you. We’re developing intelligent systems that understand location context and help users achieve what they want, wherever they are. You’ve seen our work in action through suggested locations in Maps, Journaling Suggestions for outings and trips, and curated Memories in Photos. We’re seeking motivated, experienced engineers to elevate our software’s intelligence, performance, and impact. We are looking for a seasoned engineer who can help define where this work goes next, not just how it gets built. Do you have experience linking users and devices to points of interest on a map? Are you an ML practitioner energized by the challenge of delivering rich contextual intelligence within a tight resource budget? If so, we’d love to hear from you.
As a seasoned engineer on the location technologies team, you will drive the direction for feature development and strategy. As part of this role, you'll join a team of software engineers and researchers focused on identifying behavioral patterns and you will help shape new and enhanced user experiences by collaborating closely with teams across sensing, Siri, and apps. You will partner with engineering, product, and research leadership to set a multi-year technical roadmap, translate ambiguous product goals into clear technical strategy, and make the architectural and investment trade-offs that follow.
Excited to take ownership of complex, end-to-end problems? You’ll design, build, and evaluate production ML systems that infer a device’s patterns by inference on data like GPS, Wi-Fi, and accelerometers and higher semantic signals, combining estimation techniques with machine learning. You’ll test and refine your work, use it yourself, track metrics, and iterate for quality. You will help identifing new opportunities for location intelligence across Apple’s products, and mentor engineers to raise the technical bar for the whole team.
Minimum qualifications: Experience building and shipping production software, including technical leadership of multi-engineer projects.
Experience shipping production software for mobile and/or other resource-constrained devices. Tight memory, CPU, and schedule constraints motivate you and ignite your creativity. Capability of creating, analyzing, and modifying SW functionality, ideally in C++/Obj-C/Swift codebases.
Data processing: Skilled in working with large, noisy datasets.
Experience with libraries like NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, and PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Hands-on experience with applied probability, statistics, and empirical and/or ML algorithms. Classical estimation, signal processing, and/or training supervised ML models are relevant.
Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
Preferred qualifications: Proven track record of setting technical strategy and roadmaps for ML-driven product features, and of influencing decisions across organizations without direct authority.
Machine Learning algorithms: Strong grasp of supervised/unsupervised learning, regression, classification, clustering, and model evaluation techniques.
Having worked as an ML practitioner in an industrial setting.
Experience mentoring and growing engineers, and building alignment among technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Laser focus on customer impact and product experience.
Some professional background in location and/or other wireless sensing technologies, including for example, GPS/GNSS, WiFi, indoor localization, and/or discrete localization.
Excellent communication, verbally and in writing. You can present strategy and technical trade-offs clearly to senior leadership. You can succeed in a collaborative environment, and are comfortable with what will sometimes feel like a high degree of uncertainty.
You can innovate within tight memory, CPU, and schedule constraints, and deliver on time. These constraints motivate you and ignite your creativity.

title: Software Engineer, Automations and Shortcuts, Proactive
description:
Play a part in the next revolution in human-computer interaction. Join the team behind Shortcuts, Siri, and Proactive Intelligence technology that helps millions of people get more done on their devices, privately and securely. As an iOS and macOS engineer on this team, you'll help shape Automations and the connected home experience, turning smart devices into something truly intelligent. You'll ship code that runs on the devices you use every day, as part of a collaborative team building a first-party app across all of Apple's platforms.
You'll focus on Automations the system that lets people connect their apps, devices, and home accessories into seamless, intelligent routines. Experience building software applications in Objective-C or Swift
Skilled communicator, both verbally and in writing

title: Software Engineer, Contacts
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job, and there’s no telling what you could accomplish.

title: Software Engineer, Deployment Compliance
description:
Imagine empowering hundreds of developers across Apple Service Engineering to build, ship, and hotfix their services faster, more reliably, and with far less toil. At Apple, we don't just build products, we craft experiences that redefine entire ecosystems. The Build Support Engineering (BSE) team sits underneath that work, owning the build, deployment, and hotfix infrastructure that Apple's Commerce and platform engineering teams depend on to get code into production every day. Join us to develop the next-generation of Apple's cloud services infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on the Build Support Engineering team, you'll play a key role in modernizing large-scale build and deployment systems - untangling years of legacy tooling, standardizing on a single containerized build-and-deploy path, and building agentic AI systems that triage incidents, debug failures, and support developers autonomously. This is about designing robust, scalable systems that let hundreds of developers build, test, and release services efficiently, while continuously simplifying the platform underneath them. We're seeking engineers with a strong foundation in backend development who are also excited about applying AI - including agentic, tool-using systems - in practical, impactful ways. If you're energized by challenges that span distributed systems, build and deployment tooling, container orchestration, and autonomous intelligent agents, and ready to work on systems used by engineering teams across Apple, we'd love to hear from you. Join us, and help craft the future of build and deployment at Apple.
Imagine empowering hundreds of developers across Apple Service Engineering to plan, approve, and release changes to their services faster, more safely, and with far less toil.
At Apple, we don't just build products, we craft experiences that redefine entire ecosystems. The Application Change Management Services team sits underneath that work, owning the services that govern how changes reach production across Apple's platform engineering teams every day: change tracking, approvals and risk assessment, release coordination, and audit and compliance workflows. Join us to develop the next generation of Apple's cloud services infrastructure.
As a Software Engineer on the Application Change Management Services team, you'll play a key role in modernizing large-scale change management systems. You'll untangle years of legacy process and tooling, standardize on a single, well-integrated path from change request to production, and build agentic AI systems that assess change risk, triage failed or blocked changes, and support developers autonomously. This is about designing robust, scalable systems that let hundreds of developers propose, validate, and release changes efficiently, while continuously simplifying the platform underneath them.
We're seeking engineers with a strong foundation in backend development who are also excited about applying AI, including agentic, tool-using systems, in practical, impactful ways. If you're energized by challenges that span distributed systems, change and release tooling, integrations with build and deployment pipelines, and autonomous intelligent agents, and you're ready to work on systems used by engineering teams across Apple, we'd love to hear from you.
Join us, and help craft the future of change management at Apple.

Strong programming skills in Java and Python.
Familiarity with utilizing and developing AI-driven and agentic tools to improve workflows and productivity.
Knowledge of algorithms, data structures, and distributed systems principles.
Experience with databases (relational and/or NoSQL) and scalable service architectures.
Excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset.
BS, MS or PhD in Computer Science/Engineering
Preferred qualifications: Experience with containerization and standardized image-based deployment workflows.
Familiarity with AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and LLM libraries (e.g., LangChain, Hugging Face), or building AI-assisted developer and on-call tooling.

Experience with large-scale codebase migrations and multi-repo tooling.
Experience with messaging systems (e.g., Kafka) and microservices architectures.
Passion for developer experience and empathy for building tools that empower other engineers.

title: Software Engineer, Deployment Platform MultiCloud
description:
Do you love building the platforms that other engineers depend on to do their best work? Do you want to make deploying an application, from a first preview to production, a one-minute, self-service step instead of a ticket and a wait? Your work will be used by thousands of engineers across Apple every day.

Deploying an application is something developers do many times a day, and we aim to make it fast, reliable, and effortless. Strong programming skills in Go, with experience delivering high-quality, concurrent, well-tested services
Solid foundation in software architecture, system design, and problem solving

Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Self-motivated and well-organized, with a demonstrated ability to take ownership and drive ambiguous projects to completion

Familiarity with service identity, secrets management, and secure multi-tenant design
Hands-on experience with Kubernetes and cloud networking, such as ingress and egress controllers, service mesh, CNI, or Gateway API, across multi-cluster, hybrid-cloud, or ephemeral cluster environments, and with debugging networking issues across layers (DNS, TLS, proxies, load balancers)

Experience with observability: metrics, logging, tracing, and SLOs

Familiarity with virtualization and VM workloads alongside containers
Kubernetes application developer certification (CKAD)

title: Software Engineer, G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE)
description:
G&A Solutions Engineering (GSE) is IS&T's dedicated technology partner for Apple's general and administrative functions — including people, finance, facilities, legal, and security. The team builds and delivers integrated technology solutions that keep these functions running efficiently and securely at global scale. GSE also works closely with business teams to develop custom tools that improve productivity and bring greater automation and consistency to G&A operations across Apple.
As a Software Engineer you will be responsible for the technical design, coding, debugging of complex APIs & Micro services, and triaging bugs in several functional areas of the product.

3 years of hands-on experience implementing and optimizing both Relational and Non-Relational database solutions

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or relevant work experience

title: Software Engineering Technical Lead, Apple Card & Savings
description:
The Apple Card & Savings team is building the financial products that put users in control of their money. We built Apple Card to reinvent how credit cards work, and we continue to launch groundbreaking features used by millions of people every day. We are looking for a technical lead who craves the challenge of architecting mission-critical systems at scale, sets technical direction across teams, and is equally at home in a design review, a production incident, or a technical negotiation with a financial partner.
You'll lead the architecture and evolution of the distributed services that power Apple Card and Savings, while staying hands-on in code and operations. Our team operates as DevOps: we build what we run. You'll shape the architecture of our platform through deep experience operating, monitoring, and supporting it on call, and you'll set the bar for how we ship and run software — safe, progressive releases, clear service level objectives, and automation over manual toil. You'll lead large, multi-quarter efforts — including complex integrations with financial institution and payment network partners and other Apple services — from conception through production, with reliability and customer trust as non-negotiables.
As a technical leader, you'll drive technical discussions across teams and organizations, write specifications, represent Apple in technical discussions with external partners, review code and designs, mentor senior engineers, and raise the engineering bar for the team. Success in this role requires strong self-motivation, crisp and clear communication, a highly collaborative approach, and the ability to define and influence engineering strategy well beyond your own team.
Minimum qualifications: A demonstrated track record of architecting, building, and operating mission-critical distributed systems at large scale, while remaining hands-on in code.
Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs in consistency, latency, and throughput, and of data correctness patterns (e.g. idempotency, exactly-once processing, reconciliation).
Expert hands-on software development skills in Kotlin or Java.
Extensive operational experience: leading incident response, defining service level objectives (SLOs), and turning operational learnings into architectural improvements.
A track record of leading complex, cross-team projects from conception to production — including large migrations or platform changes — and driving consensus with diverse audiences such as global teams and external partners.
A testing-first approach to engineering: designing systems for testability from the outset, writing tests as an integral part of development, and defining testing strategy (unit, integration, contract, end-to-end) for complex services.

Experience using generative AI tools throughout the software development lifecycle to produce high-quality software.
Preferred qualifications: Deep expertise with Spring and with high-volume REST and/or gRPC services (server-to-server or mobile client facing).
Experience in payments, banking, or other regulated financial domains, including leading integrations with external financial partners and designing within compliance, consumer-protection, and privacy requirements (e.g. change management, separation of duties, PCI).
Experience architecting containerized, cloud-native applications (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes, AWS) designed for multi-region resilience, failover, graceful degradation, and self-healing, and validated through load and failure testing.

Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging (e.g. Kafka or equivalent event streaming) and optimizing SQL/NoSQL databases for scale (e.g. Aurora, DynamoDB).
A strong understanding of security, privacy, and cryptography for protecting sensitive customer and financial data (e.g. mTLS, PKI and certificate lifecycle management, JWT).

title: Software Quality Engineer, Retail & Marcom Engineering

Build and improve QE frameworks, tools, and infrastructure that increase engineering productivity
Design and implement scalable automation across UI, API, integration, and end-to-end testing.
