Familiarity with cloud and identity security (Azure, Entra ID, app registrations and permissions) and asset inventory or posture management.
Ability to understand business processes and connect technical findings to business and operational risk.

title: Firmware Engineer, Robotics
description:
About the Team

We are building general-purpose robotics. In the short term, we are focused on robots to support skilled workers to build our future infrastructure. In the long term, we imagine everyone having a personal robot doing anything they need. Progress is rapid, and based on a foundation of co-design between robotics hardware and ML research.

About the Role

As a Firmware Engineer, you will define and drive the architecture of embedded systems for next-generation hardware products. You will own foundational firmware decisions across real-time execution, device bring-up, hardware interfaces, fault handling, safety mechanisms, and production readiness.

We’re looking for someone with deep experience building safety-critical or high-consequence systems, where failures can have meaningful consequences. You should be comfortable reasoning about risk, designing for diagnosability and graceful degradation, and creating engineering practices that raise the reliability bar for the entire team.

You should also be unusually good at moving fast. Sometimes the right answer is a carefully reviewed architecture that will endure for years; sometimes it is getting a rough-but-useful prototype working by the end of the afternoon so the team can learn something concrete tomorrow. We value engineers who know the difference, make that call well, and can operate credibly in both modes.

You will be both a technical leader and a hands-on builder: setting direction, reviewing critical designs, unblocking the hardest problems, and writing production firmware when it matters most.

Our embedded stack uses a lot of Rust. Extensive experience in the language is a big help!

In this role, you will:

 - Rapidly bring up new hardware and set execution pace for the team.

 - Lead firmware architecture for embedded systems spanning boot, RTOS/runtime behavior, peripheral control, power management, communications, and field diagnostics.

 - Define engineering standards for reliability, fault tolerance, observability, and maintainability across the firmware stack.

 - Design and review safety-critical mechanisms, including fault detection, recovery paths, watchdog strategies, redundancy where appropriate, and safe-state behavior.

 - Build quick, scrappy prototypes when speed of learning matters, then harden the right ideas into production-quality systems.

 - Partner closely with engineers in hardware, software, and AI research from early prototype through production.

 - Build rigorous bring-up, validation, and release processes for embedded platforms.

 - Establish testing strategies across unit, hardware-in-the-loop, integration, stress, and failure-injection testing.

 - Drive root-cause analysis for subtle hardware, firmware, and system interactions.

 - Make clear tradeoffs across performance, memory, power, schedule, and safety.

 - Mentor firmware engineers and help shape a culture of urgency, technical rigor, practical judgment, and high-quality execution.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have extensive experience developing firmware in an iterative environment.

 - Get a thrill from bringing up new hardware and taking end-to-end ownership over ensuring it works.

 - Have led architecture and delivery for complex embedded products that shipped to real users or operated in demanding production environments.

 - Are deeply fluent in low-level languages (we use Rust!) and comfortable working close to hardware under real-time constraints.

 - Understand embedded systems from first principles, including interrupts, scheduling, memory layout, buses, DMA, timing behavior, and failure modes.

 - Have strong instincts for defensive design, fault containment, validation depth, and post-deployment diagnosability.

 - Know when to build the durable system and when to produce the fastest credible artifact that unlocks the next decision.

 - Communicate clearly across disciplines and can turn ambiguity into sound technical direction.

 - Care about building systems that are not only fast and capable, but also trustworthy.

 - Make heavy use of Codex, Claude Code, or similar AI-assisted coding systems to accelerate implementation, prototyping, debugging, and iteration.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with Rust in embedded environments.

 - Experience with Embassy or other async embedded Rust frameworks.

 - Familiarity with mixed-language firmware architectures, including introducing Rust incrementally into existing C/C++ systems.

 - Experience with ARM Cortex-M or Cortex-R platforms, RTOSes, and low-power embedded designs.

 - Experience building firmware for sensor-rich, latency-sensitive, or tightly integrated electromechanical products.

About the Team

The Transformation team at OpenAI partners with Finance, Infrastructure, Data, and Engineering to design and scale the business processes and systems that support our growth. Our work combines process design, systems thinking, and operational change to turn fragmented workflows into reliable, repeatable, and well-controlled operations.

We work as embedded partners to Finance, Accounting, and Operations, shaping priorities and delivering improvements across core business processes. For compute, our focus is an accurate, connected view of contractual obligations, delivered capacity, usage, and cost that supports sound decisions and repeatable financial operations.

About the Role

As Program Manager, Compute Transformation, you will lead cross-functional initiatives that connect purchasing, operations, billing, accounting, and financial planning across our compute commitments and our data center initiatives. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of problem definition, process design, integrated planning, and end-to-end delivery.

You will work across Compute Finance, Infrastructure Accounting, Capacity Planning, Fleet, Design & Construction, Operations, Procurement, Legal, Data, and Engineering. You will turn ambiguous business problems into clear requirements, drive decisions and dependencies, and deliver reliable processes and systems that make compute and infra spend easier to understand, forecast, reconcile, and control.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, with a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office.

In this role, you will:

 - Own an integrated compute and infra transformation plan: workstreams, milestones, critical dependencies, resources, decision logs, and acceptance criteria. Drive execution from problem definition through production adoption.

 - Map current workflows and design scalable processes from demand planning, contracting, delivery & acceptance, receiving & operations, invoicing, payment, and month-end close. Clarify ownership, handoffs, evidence, and exception paths.

 - Enable source of truth systems that cover both operational needs and accounting / finance needs for data center construction, operations, and maintenance.

 - Drive consistent tracking of contracts, tranches, delivery events, and capacity acceptance. Connect committed spend to provisioned, accepted, allocated, and used capacity to support forecasting and financial review.

 - Coordinate reliable ingestion and normalization of cloud service provider usage, billing, invoice, and delivery data. Establish data owners, completeness checks, and traceability to financial outputs.

 - Improve compute billing, accrual, and allocation processes through consistent pricing rules, SKU mappings, telemetry and organizational tags, reconciliations, and controlled handling of manual adjustments.

 - Partner with application, AI, and data engineers to translate requirements into integrations and automation across contract, procurement, compute data, and finance platforms, with monitoring and governed change controls.

 - Align Infrastructure, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Legal, and Engineering on decisions and dependencies. Manage scope, risks, vendor dependencies, and change requests; escalate with clear options and business impact.

 - Lead end-to-end testing, UAT, rollout, training, and handoff to operational owners. Define success measures for traceability, data quality, manual effort, exception resolution, close readiness, and adoption.

 - 8+ years of experience in project or program management, finance transformation, infrastructure operations, or enterprise systems delivery in complex, scaled environments.

 - Understanding of compute or infrastructure economics and related finance processes, including commitments, usage-based billing, procurement, accruals, cost allocation, and forecasting.

 - Experience partnering with software and data engineers to define requirements, resolve tradeoffs, test solutions, and deliver changes into production without direct authority.

 - A strong process mindset and the ability to connect contractual terms, operational events, financial data, and control requirements into a practical future-state design.

 - Fluency in data dependencies, system integrations, reconciliation, and data quality. Comfort working with analytical teams and tools such as SQL, Databricks, and BI platforms.

title: RTL Design Engineer, Networking / NoC
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for an RTL Design Engineer to help design and develop next-generation AI accelerator silicon. In this role, you'll work across architecture, microarchitecture, and RTL implementation, translating complex system and performance requirements into efficient, scalable hardware designs.

You'll collaborate closely with silicon architects, hardware and software engineers, verification, and physical design teams to co-design hardware solutions optimized for demanding AI workloads. This is a hands-on engineering role with opportunities to influence architectural decisions, drive microarchitecture development, and own RTL design from early concept through implementation and integration.

We're particularly interested in engineers with experience in Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect architectures, or high-performance data movement, though the role encompasses broader RTL design and hardware co-design challenges.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement high-performance RTL for next-generation AI accelerator silicon, from microarchitecture definition through implementation and integration.

 - Collaborate with architecture and software teams to translate system-level requirements into efficient hardware microarchitectures.

 - Drive hardware/software co-design efforts to optimize performance, power, area, and scalability for AI workloads.

 - Develop and optimize RTL for complex datapaths, control logic, interconnects, and other critical silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and microarchitectural tradeoffs across bandwidth, latency, throughput, and resource utilization.

 - Partner with design verification and formal verification teams to ensure functional correctness, develop verification strategies, and debug complex design issues.

 - Work closely with physical design teams to optimize RTL for synthesis, timing closure, power, and area.

 - Contribute to architecture reviews, design specifications, and cross-functional discussions to influence future silicon designs.

 - Support block-level and SoC-level integration, debugging, and performance optimization.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong hands-on experience with ASIC RTL design and microarchitecture development using SystemVerilog or Verilog.

 - Have experience designing and implementing complex digital hardware blocks, from architecture and specification through RTL development and verification.

 - Understand hardware architecture and microarchitecture tradeoffs, including performance, power, area, latency, and throughput.

 - Have experience collaborating across architecture, software, verification, and physical design teams to develop optimized hardware solutions.

 - Can reason about complex hardware systems, identify performance bottlenecks, and translate architectural requirements into efficient RTL implementations.

 - Have experience with synthesis, timing closure, and physical implementation considerations.

 - Enjoy working on ambiguous, technically challenging problems and taking ownership of designs from concept through integration.

 - Bring experience with Network-on-Chip (NoC), networking, interconnect fabrics, packet-based architectures, or high-bandwidth data movement systems.

 - Experience with AI accelerators, high-performance computing, or hardware/software co-design is a plus.

OpenAI's Marketing team helps people understand and use AI responsibly. We work with Research, Product, Design, Communications, and Creative to turn complex capabilities into clear stories, useful examples, and experiences that help audiences understand what the technology can do.

About the Role

As a Research Product Marketing Manager, you will help translate OpenAI's research into accurate positioning, compelling demonstrations, and launch narratives. You will work closely with researchers and product teams to understand new capabilities, the evidence behind them, and their limitations, then explain why they matter to the audiences we want to reach.

You will connect technical understanding with audience insight, carrying work from the initial brief through launch and follow-through. This is a hands-on role for a marketer who can ask precise questions, write clearly, and help teams make sound decisions as research and product plans evolve.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop positioning and messaging for research capabilities and releases, grounding claims in evidence and clearly distinguishing demonstrated results from possible applications.

 - Partner with researchers and product leads to understand how capabilities work, where they are useful, and what limitations or caveats audiences need to know.

 - Define priority audiences and questions for each initiative. Use research, feedback, and usage signals to identify barriers to understanding and opportunities for useful adoption.

 - Build launch briefs that connect the research story, audience needs, communications goals, and the work required from cross-functional partners.

location: Palo Alto, California, United States; San Francisco, California, United States
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Strategic Finance Manager
This role reports into the Head of Corporate Finance/FP&A and serves as a senior strategic finance partner to leadership across the business. The ideal candidate brings a strong foundation in investment banking and corporate finance, with experience supporting complex, high-growth businesses—ideally within eCommerce, consumer, or other fast-paced, technology-enabled environments. They demonstrate advanced analytical judgment and deep expertise in financial modeling, forecasting, and strategic analysis, along with fluency in Excel, financial planning systems, and data visualization tools.
This individual is expected to independently lead high-visibility financial initiatives, translate data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership, and serve as a trusted thought partner to cross-functional stakeholders. Success in this role requires comfort operating in ambiguity, a proactive problem-solving mindset, and the ability to scale processes and insights alongside a rapidly growing business. This person is required to be in office 4 days a week in San Francisco, CA or Palo Alto, CA.
Responsibilities
Serve as a strategic finance partner to senior leadership, owning forecasting, long-range planning, and performance analysis across key areas of the business.
Build and maintain sophisticated financial models to support strategic decisions, including scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and business case development.
Lead the annual operating plan and quarterly re-forecast processes, driving alignment on assumptions, targets, and resource allocation.
Partner cross-functionally with teams across the company to translate operational drivers into financial outcomes and identify opportunities to improve profitability and efficiency.
Develop and track key company KPIs and unit economics, connecting operational performance to broader financial outcomes such as contribution margin, cash flow, and enterprise value.
Prepare and evolve Weekly Business Review (WBR) and board-level materials, synthesizing complex analyses into clear, actionable narratives for executive leadership and investors.
Deliver high-impact ad hoc analyses on strategic initiatives, investments, pricing, and growth opportunities to inform decision-making.
Drive continuous improvement in financial processes, reporting infrastructure, and planning systems to scale with the business.
Qualifications
Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related discipline.
4 - 8 years of progressive experience, ideally combining investment banking or corporate finance with FP&A, strategic finance, or a similar role supporting complex, operationally intensive businesses, preferably in retail, consumer, eCommerce, or supply chain driven environments.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a trusted strategic finance partner, influencing decisions through strong cross-functional collaboration with operational, commercial, and technical teams.
Deep expertise in financial modeling, scenario analysis, and business case development, with a track record of evaluating tradeoffs and informing high-impact decisions.
Strong understanding of unit economics and customer economics, including contribution margin drivers, cost structures, and the financial implications of operational and growth investments.
Advanced proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets, including complex models and sensitivity analyses, along with hands-on experience using financial planning and reporting systems (e.g., Adaptive, Anaplan, Hyperion, NetSuite, or similar tools).
Solid command of accounting and finance fundamentals, including GAAP, general ledger review, and financial controls, with the ability to partner effectively with Accounting teams.
Exceptional analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize large, complex data sets into clear insights that influence executive decision-making.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting structured financial narratives and recommendations to senior leadership.
High attention to detail paired with the ability to manage competing priorities and ambiguity in a fast-paced, scaling environment.
A proactive, intellectually curious mindset, with the confidence to challenge assumptions, identify risks and opportunities, and propose thoughtful, data-backed solutions.
Preferred:
Master's Degree (MBA) or relevant certifications (e.g., CFA)
Investment banking and/or private equity experience
Finance experience in a retail, e-commerce, consumer goods, or supply chain–driven industry

Role Summary Join Rivian’s Vehicle Hardware Engineering — Chassis — Product Development team as the Staff (Lead) Steering Engineer for Chassis. This RIV-6 role will provide technical leadership for the development and integration of steering systems and hardware across Rivian vehicle programs, from early concept through production release, launch, and engineering sign-off. You will own complex steering system and component decisions, define and cascade technical requirements, lead cross-functional execution, and serve as a trusted technical escalation point for steering design, validation, supplier, and production issues. Your scope may include steering columns, intermediate shafts, dash seals, electric power-assisted steering racks and gears, tie rods, fasteners, and next-generation mechatronic systems such as steer-by-wire, rear-wheel steering, and advanced ADAS steering technologies. The successful candidate combines deep steering engineering expertise with strong systems thinking, sound first-principles judgment, and the ability to lead through influence. You will help shape steering technology strategy, raise engineering standards, mentor other engineers, and deliver a confident, connected driving experience on every surface and in every condition. Reports to: Senior Manager, Chassis — Steering, Wheels & Tires Responsibilities Spearhead End-to-End Architecture & Development: Lead the technical direction and hardware development for complex steering systems—including advanced Steer-by-Wire (SbW)—making critical architecture decisions that balance safety, performance, NVH, cost, and manufacturability across vehicle programs. Manage the Requirements Lifecycle: Author and translate vehicle-level customer attributes into detailed system and component specifications. Drive cross-functional alignment with Vehicle Dynamics, Controls, Functional Safety, Software, and ADAS, while proactively mitigating downstream design impacts. Drive Clean-Sheet Design & Optimization: Utilize first-principles engineering, CATIA V6 / 3DEXPERIENCE, CAE, and data-driven trade studies to optimize designs, oversee kinematic packaging, and identify opportunities for improved robustness and customer experience. Define robust duty cycles, test methods, and acceptance criteria to ensure comprehensive coverage of system durability, performance, and failure modes. Lead Advanced Problem-Solving: Resolve complex, ambiguous, and systemic steering issues from containment through root cause analysis and prevention. Establish reusable problem-solving methodologies and decisively communicate technical conclusions. Direct Supplier Technical Development: Hold suppliers accountable to strict quality, timing, and engineering deliverables. Partner with Purchasing to review supplier designs and test plans to achieve the optimal total system solution. Represent Steering in Gateway Reviews: Act as the technical authority for Steering Engineering in design reviews, program gateways, build events, and leadership forums, presenting clear recommendations, risks, trade-offs, and recovery plans. Champion Engineering Standards: Create, improve, and enforce steering design rules, validation practices, and development methodologies to elevate engineering rigor across the broader Chassis organization. Mentor and Elevate the Team: Coach less-experienced engineers through design reviews, technical problem-solving, and supplier engagement to raise the overall quality and consistency of steering deliverables. Manage Concurrent Workstreams: Balance multiple vehicle programs and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment. Travel as required to support supplier visits, physical testing, prototype builds, and production launches. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. 7+ years of relevant experience in automotive steering system or hardware development at an OEM, steering supplier, or equivalent engineering organization Demonstrated experience leading steering engineering work across multiple vehicle development programs, including concept, development, validation, launch, and production support. Deep technical knowledge of mechanical steering systems and components, including steering columns, intermediate shafts, seals, EPAS racks/gears, tie rods, joints, fasteners, and steering interfaces. Experience owning or leading system-level and component-level requirements, DFMEA, DVP&R/DVPR, validation planning, design release, engineering change, and sign-off activities. Strong first-principles problem-solving capability, including root-cause analysis, structured corrective action, and data-driven decision making under uncertainty. Experience with CATIA V6 / 3DEXPERIENCE or an equivalent production CAD environment, along with CAE/FEA tools and engineering release systems. Working knowledge of chassis design, vehicle dynamics, steering performance, materials, manufacturing processes, GD&T, design for manufacturing, and joint/fastener engineering. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical decisions, resolve conflicts, influence without direct authority, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, suppliers, and leadership. Demonstrated leadership aptitude, including mentoring engineers, reviewing technical work, setting a high bar for engineering rigor, and representing a functional area in cross-functional forums. Experience working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments with compressed timing and multiple concurrent priorities. Champion emerging AI advancements and translate state-of-the-art tech into transformative, real-world operational advantages

title: Assembly Technician
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll build the robots that are showing up on factory floors across the country. Standard Bots is moving fast from prototype to high-volume production, and the people on the assembly line are the most important people in the building — this role sits right at the center of that. You'll work alongside the Production Supervisor and the engineering team, turning parts into precision robotic systems that are ready to work.

📍 Location

This is a full-time, on-site role at our Glen Cove, NY manufacturing facility, working first shift, Monday through Friday. We're unable to sponsor visas for this role.


What you'll do

- Assemble production robots and components to spec, following work instructions — hands-on work that takes a pile of parts and turns it into a finished machine.

- Run quality checks throughout the build, not just at the end, and report issues to the Production Supervisor as soon as you spot them.

- Keep your workspace safe and organized, in line with company and industry standards.

- Handle material movement and distribution to workstations so the line keeps running.

- Contribute to continuous improvement on the production floor — if you see a better way to build, we want to hear it.


What you'll bring

- A high school diploma or equivalent.

- 2+ years in a mass production or manufacturing environment.

- 1+ year of hands-on assembly, maintenance/repair, or tool experience.

- The ability to lift up to 50 lbs.

- Sharp attention to detail — you catch things, and you don't let things slide.

- Clear communication: you flag issues quickly and work well within a team.

- The ability to prioritize and stay focused when things are moving fast.

- A habit of showing up every shift ready to execute, and pride in clean, accurate assembly work.


Nice to have

- An Associate's or Bachelor's degree.

- Experience in automotive, aerospace, industrial, or electromechanical manufacturing.

- Machine shop or CNC equipment experience.

- Familiarity with OSHA standards and workplace safety practices.


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $30.00 to $36.00 per hour, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Mechanical Engineer - Sensor Cleaning
description:
As a Mechanical Engineer on the Sensor Cleaning team, you will design, validate and launch hardware systems that keep our camera, lidar, radar and other autonomy sensors operating at their best regardless of the environmental conditions we operate in. You will own components and systems end to end: from developing proofs of concept, vehicle integration, design and release, to validation in our climatic wind tunnel and across our fleet. You will drive solutions that maximize sensor performance, improve vehicle availability, and support scalable deployment of Zoox autonomous vehicles. In this role, you will:

Design and development

  • Develop sensor cleaning components and systems to manage debris, rain, and snow across our global operations.
  • Design and build mockups, proofs of concept and functional prototypes; develop packaging studies to support vehicle integration.
  • Develop and release CAD, engineering drawings and BOMs supported by tolerance analysis, DFMEA, DFM/DFA and reliability assessments.

    • Validation and testing

  • Collaborate with our validation team on test plans, test fixtures design, and testing failure analysis.
  • Support wind tunnel and fleet testing of sensor cleaning functionality.

    • Fleet support and production

  • Own your hardware performance in the field. Diagnose and troubleshoot fleet issues affecting sensor cleaning performance.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing and quality engineers to ramp production processes and meet build objectives.

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering or Mechatronics 
  • Strong mechanical design fundamentals: plastic injection-molded components, sheet metal and machined parts, fluid and pneumatic systems, or thermal and heating system integration.
  • Proficiency with 3D CAD (CATIA, NX, Creo or SolidWorks).
  • Familiarity with data acquisition tools. Inquisitive
  • Hands-on experience troubleshooting mechanical and electrical failures.
  • Basic understanding of Python or another scripting language.
  • Experience leading cross-functional teams to drive new ideas and solutions into products.
    • Bonus qualifications
  • Experience with automotive sensors (camera, lidar) or optical sensor/ADAS systems.
  • Experience with hydraulic and pneumatic systems.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Autonomy Safety Metric
description:
We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced engineer to join the Behavior Evaluation team and play a pivotal role in measuring the safety of Zoox’s autonomous driving technology. The Behavior Evaluation is the team behind the behavioral part of Zoox’s ADPIES estimate, quantifying how often the autonomy stack causes the vehicle to stop unexpectedly and how that maps to collision risk. As a member of this team, you will own and scale the pipeline behind these numbers, driving innovation in ML model scoring, sampling, and projections while making the system faster, more reliable, and easier to audit. You will work closely with a team of talented engineers and researchers in a fast paced, collaborative environment as Zoox expands to more cities and software releases. In this role, you will:

  • Build and maintain the Behavior Evaluation data pipelines (PySpark/zspark medallion architecture on Databricks, EMR Serverless and Airflow) that produce weekly per-geofence estimates.

  • Turn the statistical method (sampling, triage weights, mileage sharing, projections) into tested, reproducible code with checks that fail loudly when the data is bad.

  • Build tools that cut the manual work in each weekly run.

  • Work with cross functional stakeholders so the methodology is applied consistently in code and in clearance reports.

  • Help adapt to new release methodologies and new geofences.

    • Qualifications:

  • 7 - 9 Years of experience or 5+ years with a strong data-platform track record 

  • Expert Python, with production experience in PySpark/Spark and Pandas

  • Experience designing scalable batch data pipelines: orchestration, Delta/lakehouse tables, idempotent backfills

  • Solid grounding in applied statistics: sampling, weighting, estimators, confidence intervals

  • Strong testing and CI habits for data code

    • Bonus Qualifications:

  • Experience with autonomous-vehicle simulation, safety metrics or triage workflows

  • Experience putting ML models into production in a data pipeline 

  • Experience with Databricks and AWS (EMR Serverless, S3)

    • Accommodations If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to accommodations@zoox.com or your assigned recruiter.   A Final Note: You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. title: Team Lead, Readiness & Response
description:
As a Team Lead for Readiness and Response within Zoox’s Fleet Operations organization, you are at the forefront of the autonomous mobility revolution. You will be a key leader in our expansion into new markets, responsible for the end-to-end operational integrity of the Zoox Robotaxi and Mapping Vehicle Fleet. This role unifies the technical preparation of our vehicles (Readiness) with high-level oversight of live field incidents (Response), ensuring every Zoox vehicle is "service ready" and every mission is supported with operational excellence. Your leadership will bridge the gap between structured depot workflows and the dynamic environment of real-time fleet response. Rather than performing hands-on technical tasks, you will drive strategy and performance by managing a hybrid workforce of Full-Time Shift Leads and contingent associates. Serving as the primary on-site escalation path for critical field incidents and holding third-party recovery partners accountable, you will directly impact Zoox’s fleet availability, safety standards, and our ability to deliver a seamless experience to our riders.   Shift: 1st Shift, 7am - 4pm, Tuesday - Saturday   Travel Requirements: less than 20% In this role, you will:
  • Collaborate with Leadership: Work with Fleet Ops leaders in market, as well as Fleet Ops Program Teams, to ensure optimization of fleet utilization while driving market needs.
  • Drive Unified Fleet Strategy: Oversee the execution of operational strategies for both vehicle preparation (Readiness) and incident response (Response), ensuring alignment with broader organizational uptime goals.
  • Lead through Shift Leadership: Directly manage and mentor FTE Shift Leads & a contingent workforce, empowering them to oversee daily floor operations while you focus on high-level strategy, performance coaching, and site-wide operational health.
  • Manage On-Site Escalations: Serve as the primary leadership escalation path for critical field incidents and service interferences, providing guidance to the team and making high-level decisions to resolve complex vehicle or rider issues.
  • Manage a Hybrid Workforce: Provide administrative and people leadership for a multidisciplinary team, including onboarding, training, and performance management for contingent (contract) workforces.
  • Coordinate Third-Party Vendors On The Ground: Serve as the local point of contact for vehicle recovery, roadside assistance, and facility vendors — verifying on-site service quality and response time, and flagging no-shows, defects, or service misses to the relevant Program team, who owns vendor standards, governance, and corrective action.
  • Optimize Operational Workflows: Identify bottlenecks in depot workflows (software deployment, sensor cleaning), field response protocols, and work with cross-functional partners to implement process innovations to reduce vehicle downtime.
  • Ensure Regulatory & Safety Compliance: Oversee adherence to all health and safety policies (OSHA) within the workshop and ensure all vehicle documentation and "Up/Down" status reporting are accurate and audit-ready.
  • Synthesize Operational Data: Own the analysis and reporting of site-specific KPIs, providing leadership with data-driven insights into fleet health, team efficiency, and vendor performance.
    • Qualifications
  • 8+ years of relevant work experience in an operations-based environment
  • Experience Managing People Leaders: Demonstrated ability to manage and develop direct reports at the Shift Lead or Supervisor level.
  • Contingent Workforce Management: Extensive experience leading, onboarding, and managing the performance of contractor or contingent workforces.
  • Vendor & Partner Management: Demonstrated experience managing 3rd party service providers and holding external partners accountable to Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
  • Critical Thinking under Pressure: Ability to manage high-priority escalations and make sound, data-driven decisions in fast-paced or ambiguous situations.
  • Technical Aptitude: Ability to understand complex technical systems (autonomous vehicle hardware/software) to effectively lead technical teams and communicate with engineering stakeholders.
  • Process Improvement Mindset: Experience facilitating Lean Six Sigma projects or similar methodologies to improve operational efficiency.
  • Safety Excellence: Commitment to maintaining a culture of safety and compliance; must have a clean driving record.

  • Experience with autonomous vehicles, or a similar safety-critical industry
  • Experience in a fast-paced and dynamic service environment.
  • Experience with Lean Six Sigma or other process optimization methodologies.
  • Familiarity with fleet management software.
